## 14 Nov 2026 - Round 505 (E525): the replay no longer runs in the live container and no longer keeps a whole recorded day in memory

 * **VM run of round 504 (14 Nov): the replay was killed with exit 137 and the live `fno-options-service` restarted** (`docker compose ps` showed the container created 38 seconds earlier). Cause: round 503's wrapper ran the replay with `docker compose exec` INSIDE the live container, and `replay.run` kept every parsed snapshot of both underlyings of a day in memory (a snapshot is a whole option chain) while `ReplayProvider` rebuilt a list of all snapshots so far on every tick, so the memory limit killed it. It was a Saturday; on a trading day this would have stopped the engine. I should have caught this in round 503: running a heavy job in the live service container was the wrong design.
 * **Changed: `scripts/fno_replay_vm.sh`** runs the replay in its OWN throw-away container (`docker run --rm`) made from the same image: recordings mounted read-only, this checkout's `services/fno-options-service` mounted read-only over `/app` (no image rebuild needed), `--network none`, hard memory cap `--memory 3g --memory-swap 3g` (`REPLAY_MEM=5g` to change). Result files go to `./data/fno_real_probe/replay_out/backtests/` on the host. It prints the size of every recorded day first, and on exit 137 says that only the replay container ran out of memory and the live service is untouched. (The result is no longer written to `/data/fno/backtests`, so the F&O tab does not list it; the text report is printed.)
 * **Changed: `backtest/replay.py` and `fno/recorder.py`.** New `recorder.index_day` (one line parsed at a time; keeps ts, byte offset, spot, vix, expiry; the same lines skipped as `read_day`) and `recorder.read_at`; new `_SnapIndex`; `ReplayProvider` finds the newest snapshot at a time with bisect and parses a snapshot only when the engine asks for its chain (small cache), builds the 5-minute bars incrementally, and finds the latest VIX with bisect. Same results as before: on a synthetic three-day, two-underlying recording the old and the new code give byte-identical trades (checked by running both trees); peak memory fell from 92 MB to 31 MB on that small recording (real chains are far larger, so the gain is larger), and it is no longer quadratic in the number of snapshots. `ReplayProvider` still accepts plain lists of snapshot dicts, so the existing tests are unchanged. `recorder.read_day` is unchanged (the engine tests and other callers use it). 5 new tests in `tests/test_round505_replay_index.py`, 2 wrapper tests in `scripts/test_fno_export_candles.py` (a fake `docker`: the replay is `docker run`, never `compose exec`, with the cap, the read-only mounts and `--network none`).
 * Not changed: no order-path code. The memory growth of the live recorder itself is not touched.

## 14 Nov 2026 - Round 498 (E518): F&O - the stop is never inside the option's own daily noise

 * **Round 498 (E518):** item 3 of the 13 Nov review ("the 25 % stop sits inside normal option-price noise"; a hypothesis, NOT_PROVEN: the repo holds no option-premium noise measurement, so the numbers below are my choice, not a fitted value). A flat 25 % is wide for a 150-rupee option and tight for a 60-rupee one, because the same index move is a bigger % of a cheaper premium. New `sizing.noise_stop_pct` / `with_noise_stop`: the stop % for one entry is `FNO_SL_NOISE_ATR_FRAC` (default 0.20) x delta x the 14-day daily ATR (spot points, `bias["atr"]`) / premium x 100, held between `FNO_SL_PCT` (25) and `FNO_SL_MAX_PCT` (default 35). Example, NIFTY ATR 300, delta 0.5: premium 150 gives 20 % -> stays 25; premium 100 gives 30; premium 60 gives 50 -> capped 35. It only ever widens (never below `FNO_SL_PCT`), 0 turns it off, and with no ATR, no premium or no delta it falls back to the plain stop (a missing delta reads as 0.5). The wider % is used for BOTH the stop price and the lot count, so the rupee risk per trade is unchanged and the lots shrink (a 30 % stop takes about 17 % fewer lots than a 25 % one). Applied in `Engine._enter` (real delta from the contract pick), the DEMO / REAL stop order carries the widened price as before, and in the three simulators (`sim.py`, `rolling_sim.py`, `eod.py`; delta is not known there, so at the money 0.5; a per-entry copy of the params is used so the stop cannot ratchet wider from entry to entry). The reconcile path that rebases a stop on an unknown entry's real fill now keeps the % that entry was given instead of resetting it to `FNO_SL_PCT`. Both new settings are live-tunable control-catalog flags with `shipped` and `recommended` values, read in `config.py` and `liveparams.py`, listed in `docker-compose.yml` and `docs/ENV_REFERENCE.txt`; `param_problems` refuses a noise fraction outside 0-2 or a widest stop outside 0-100. Tests: new `tests/test_round498_noise_stop.py` (10, one of them a full engine entry with the floor off and on). F&O suite in the sandbox: 765 passed, 1 skipped. Not run: Docker, the VM, a backtest over real history. Expect: fewer lots on low-priced options, fewer stop-outs on noise, and a larger loss per stopped trade in % of premium (the rupee loss is the same). Check the effect with `python -m backtest ... --set sl_noise_atr_frac=0` against the default before trusting it.

## 12 Nov 2026 - Round 481 (E501): a typo in a circuit-breaker or price-cap setting no longer stops the gateway, and an open circuit loaded without a timestamp now recovers

 * **Round 481 (E501):** read of the `_cb_get` / `_cb_post` / `_log_circuit_skip` / `_env_*` helpers in `main.py` (the "unread" item E500 listed) and of `circuit_breaker.py`, which they sit on. Eight defects, all reproduced first. **(1) Import-time crash.** `circuit_breaker.py` read `CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD`, `CB_HALF_OPEN_SUCCESS` and `CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT` with bare `int()` / `float()` at import, so one typo (`abc`, `1.5`) stopped the whole gateway from booting; `MAX_UNIVERSE_PRICE` / `VALUE_BUY_THRESHOLD` in `main.py` did the same (`MAX_STOCK_PRICE=\u20b9500`). A blank `MAX_UNIVERSE_PRICE` also hid a set `MAX_STOCK_PRICE` (`os.getenv(name, other)` only falls back when the variable is UNSET); the fallback now applies to blank too, as the comment above those lines always said. **(2) `CB_REDIS_MIN_INTERVAL=x`** raised ValueError out of `allow()` (and `record_success` / `record_failure`, inside the except handler of `_cb_get`, hiding the real error) on every guarded call once `CB_REDIS_SYNC=1`. **(3) `CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT=nan` / `inf`** (also the constructor argument) meant `now - opened >= timeout` was never true: an open circuit never reached half_open. **(4) Open with no timestamp.** The shared-Redis load sets `_state` from the `state` key and `_opened_at` from a separate key; with `state=open` and no `opened_at` the circuit stayed open for ever (`allow()` False, `retry_after()` 0.0 - reproduced). ## 12 Nov 2026 - Round 471 (E491): SIGTERM no longer hangs the gateway under the pinned uvicorn, and two start-up / shut-down edge cases are closed

 * **Round 471 (E491):** read of `_start_shared_http`, `_gateway_runtime_tuning`, `startup_event`, `_warm_surprise_scan_cache`, `_warm_momentum_movers_cache`, `_start_structure_refresh` / `_start_structure_refresh_locked`, `_structure_refresh_catchup_loop` and its starter / stopper, `_graceful_shutdown`, `_graceful_shutdown_commit`, `_install_signal_handlers`, `_quiet_noisy_loggers` and `_cleanup_scan_resources` (round 470 read a batch and changed nothing, so there is no E491 before this one). Three defects. **(1) `_install_signal_handlers`** replaced whatever SIGTERM / SIGINT handler was installed before it. uvicorn imports `main` either before it installs its own handlers (ours is then overwritten and only runs once, after shutdown, which is what uvicorn 0.54 does) or inside its signal capture (uvicorn 0.30.x, the version pinned in `requirements.txt` and used by the Dockerfile `CMD`, as far as I know: 0.30.1 is not installed in this sandbox, so that ordering was reproduced by driving `uvicorn.Server` directly, not by running 0.30.1). In the second order the gateway handler overwrote uvicorn's `Server.handle_exit`: SIGTERM ran the commit and then nothing told uvicorn to stop, so the process stayed up until the container runtime sent SIGKILL (reproduced: still running 6 s after SIGTERM and SIGINT, on the round 469 code). Each handler now remembers the one it replaced and calls it after the commit, so uvicorn starts its normal shutdown (lifespan shutdown hooks, then exit). SIG_DFL, SIG_IGN and Python's default SIGINT handler are not chained, so the first order behaves exactly as before. **(2) `_cleanup_scan_resources`** read `WATCHLIST_SCAN_GRACE_SECONDS` with a bare `float()` outside any try; a value such as `30s` raised out of the cleanup thread before the thread pool and the HTTP client were released, leaking both after every watchlist scan. A bad value now means the 30 s default. **(3) `_start_structure_refresh_locked`** set the job to `running` and then started the worker thread; if the thread could not start (`RuntimeError: can't start new thread`) the job stayed `running`, so every later start and the catch-up loop saw "running" and backed off. The job is now set to `error` first and the error still reaches `_start_structure_refresh`, which answers `{"ok": False, "status": "error"}` as before. Tests: new `tests/test_e491_shutdown_signal_chain_and_cleanup.py` (9 tests, run with pytest or directly, no fastapi needed: 5 fail on the E490 code: chaining after the commit, chaining after a failing commit, a real uvicorn subprocess that has to exit after SIGTERM, the bad grace value, the thread that cannot start; 4 pin unchanged behaviour: SIG_DFL / SIG_IGN / the default SIGINT handler are not chained, a failing `getsignal` still installs the handler, good grace values, a thread that starts still answers `running`). The 5 existing `_install_signal_handlers` tests in `tests/test_main_hot_run_tail.py` and the 3 `_cleanup_scan_resources` tests in `tests/test_main_scoring.py` import `main.py` and could not run here (no `fastapi` / `httpx` in this sandbox: the whole gateway suite gives 68 failed / 561 errors from that on both the E490 and the E491 tree, and 4732 -> 4741 passed with the new file); read against the new code they still hold (`getsignal` is not stubbed by the fixture, and under pytest the previous handlers are SIG_DFL and the default SIGINT handler, neither chained). Run them on the VM: `tests/test_main_hot_run_tail.py`, `tests/test_main_scoring.py`, `tests/test_e447_feed_start_guard_round427.py`, `tests/test_group360_structure_refresh.py`. On the VM, `docker stop` on the gateway should now log "Graceful shutdown complete" and exit well inside the 10 s grace period. Looked at, not changed: `_start_shared_http` (heal wait is bounded and a NaN / non-positive `BOOT_HEAL_TIMEOUT_S` falls back to 15 s; the limiter, breaker reset and holiday check are each guarded); `_gateway_runtime_tuning` (a replaced default executor is never shut down, but it is replaced once at boot); `startup_event` (8 s budget on the indices warm); `_warm_surprise_scan_cache` / `_warm_momentum_movers_cache` (the movers `finally` always sets the event, so the surprise warm never waits the full 120 s after a movers failure); `_structure_refresh_catchup_loop` (`structure_refresh._env_float` falls back on a bad value and floors the interval at 60 s, so the loop cannot spin or die on a typo); `_graceful_shutdown` (every step guarded; the commit is idempotent, so the extra commit uvicorn 0.54 triggers after shutdown is harmless); `_quiet_noisy_loggers` (the filter is added once). Not read yet: the route bodies in `gateway_support/bound_routes_*.py`.

## 12 Nov 2026 - Round 467 (E488): the bulk quote helper no longer lets a NaN price through, and the movers fallback ignores an infinite day change

 * **Round 467 (E488):** read of `_compute_momentum_movers` (all four sources, the empty-result backoff and the cache write) and of `data_feed.bulk_yahoo_download_prices`, which its fallback seed scan reads. The function itself was already well covered (E450, E473 and earlier rounds); two small gaps of the NaN / inf class remained. **(1) `bulk_yahoo_download_prices`** took the price as `float(q.get("price") or q.get("cmp") or 0)`. A NaN price (Python's JSON reader accepts `NaN`) is truthy, and `nan <= 0` and `nan > cap` are both False, so the row passed both checks with price NaN instead of falling back to a valid `cmp` or being skipped. A zero `price` next to a valid `cmp` also gets that `cmp` in the record now. **(2) Step 4 of `_compute_momentum_movers`** added a symbol when `abs(day_change_pct) >= 5`; an infinite change (previous close 0) passed that test. It now needs a finite change. New `tests/test_e488_bulk_quote_nan_price_and_infinite_change.py` (5 tests, run with pytest or directly; uses the real `data_feed` with a fake httpx): 4 fail on the E487 code, 1 pins unchanged behaviour. ## 11 Nov 2026 - Round 445 (E466): the Real Money Calibration preset no longer cancels a market-state overlay, and two crashes in the switch engine are answers

 * **Round 445 (E466):** continues the audit of `control/kit.py` (a second, closer pass over the file round 444 read; all four copies changed together and stay byte-identical). The remaining Hot Picks list is now empty (item 1 was kept as designed in round 444). Three defects, each reproduced against the real module first. **(1) The preset judged an overlaid switch against today's tightened value.** `preset_recommended` compared the RUNNING value with the recommended one. While a market-state overlay is in force, the running value is the overlay's. A switch whose SAVED value already was the recommended one (saved 10, recommended 10, overlay 5) therefore showed in the dry run as a change `5 -> 10` marked LOOSENS, and applying it with `confirm=true` went through `set()`, which cancelled the overlay and put the switch back to 10: the day's tightening was undone on exactly the kind of day it exists for. Now, while a switch is overlaid, the preset compares the SAVED value (the rule `set()` and `describe()` already use): nothing to change, the overlay stays. A saved value that differs from the recommended one is still moved, judged against the saved value (saved 20 -> 10 is a TIGHTENS), and that move still cancels the overlay because a person's change always wins. **(2) An unreadable old numeric value raised.** `classify` did `float(old)` unguarded. `running_value` falls back to the raw text of the config attribute when it cannot make it canonical (a `None` attribute gives the text `None`), so `set()` on such a switch (and the preset's dry run) ended in a `ValueError`, HTTP 500, although the docstring says an unknown old value counts as NEUTRAL. It now returns NEUTRAL for an old value that is not a number (and for NaN), so a person's change is accepted and audited as before. The bool, enum and time branches already tolerated this. **(3) A bad `until` was a 500.** `_parse_until` only caught `ValueError` from the ISO parse: a number such as `1e30` or `NaN` (Python's JSON reader accepts it) and an ISO time such as `0001-01-01T00:00:00+05:30` raised `OverflowError` or `ValueError` out of the conversion to UTC. All of them are now the same HTTP 400 with the existing message. A valid `until` is unchanged. Tests: four new cases in `scripts/test_control_kit.py` (preset keeps the overlay, preset still moves a differing saved value and judges it against the saved one, unreadable old value is NEUTRAL and `set()` works on it, bad `until` values are 400); all four fail on the round 444 code. Run here (plain-assert mode, no pytest needed): `test_control_kit.py` 29 passed, `test_regime_overlay.py` 19 passed, `test_control_snapshot.py` 5 passed, `check_control_catalog.py` and `check_shared_copies.py` ok. The service pytest suites were not run (no pytest in this sandbox). Looked at, not changed: a second `overlay_set` call with an earlier `until` than the first replaces the single state stamp, so when it expires the trade stamp goes empty while the first call's tighter switches are still in force until their own time (needs a decision: one stamp per overlay, or refuse a shorter `until`); `preset_recommended` applies its changes one `set()` at a time, so a failure part-way leaves the earlier ones applied (each is audited).

## 11 Nov 2026 - Round 443 (E464): Stop ends the Yahoo phase of the bulk feed within half a second, and a late progress write no longer undoes a Stop

 * **Round 443 (E464):** items 2 and 3 of the round 442 list (both on the Data Feed Stop path). **Item 3:** `run_bulk_yahoo_price_feed` (data_feed.py) did its Yahoo phase as one blocking `bulk_yahoo_download_prices` call (a POST /quotes/bulk with a 60 s timeout) and only looked at the stop flag before it, so Stop could take up to a minute there. The call now runs through a new `_bulk_download_interruptible` (worker thread + polling the stop flag every 0.5 s): on Stop the run returns `status: "stopped"` ("Stopped during Yahoo phase - n/total seeded") within about half a second, with the bhavcopy rows already written kept and the dropped download not written; a stop that is set as the download finishes also drops its result. The abandoned download thread is a daemon and ends on its own HTTP timeout. A download error still takes the old warning path (zero Yahoo hits, the run continues). The market-data call itself is unchanged (still one bulk POST, so no change in load or 429 risk). **Item 2:** `DataFeedStore.set_job` now ignores `status` and `message` of a PROGRESS write (status "running" without a new `started_at`) while the stop flag is set and the stored job is already "stopping" or "stopped"; its counters (processed, ok_count, ...) still update. Before, the worker's next `_progress` / resume-loop write flipped the job back to "running" over the Stop. A real start is never blocked: start writes carry `started_at`, and every start path clears the flag first. Plus one related fix: `run_bulk_yahoo_price_feed_cached` marked the bulk quote cache as a whole-universe write after a no-list run even when the run was stopped part-way; `complete` is now False for a stopped run. Not changed: the in-flight symbol of the other feed loops still finishes (item 3 was only about the single-call Yahoo phase); the guard is per process (the app runs one uvicorn process). Tests: `test_e464_stop_not_undone_and_yahoo_phase_interruptible_round443.py` (new, 12 cases: six set_job cases, stop during the download, stop as it finishes, normal write, download error, the helper, the cache flag). Run here without pytest (not installed in this sandbox): the helper and the set_job guard were exercised directly against the real module (stop during a download returned in 0.5 s; a progress write after Stop kept "stopping"); the pytest files are unrun.

## 11 Nov 2026 - Round 442 (E463): the retry pause in the scan worker no longer holds a scan slot, and a 4xx is not retried

 * **Round 442 (E463):** item 4 of the round 441 list (the same shape as E416, which fixed the circuit-open lane). In `_analyze_one_symbol_ultra` (api-gateway/main.py) the whole retry loop ran inside `async with sem`, so the `RETRY_BACKOFF` sleep (1 s) before the second attempt held one of the `MAX_PARALLEL_WORKERS` scan slots, and a slow or failing decision service lowered scan throughput for every other symbol. A 4xx answer (a bad symbol, a 404, a 422) was also asked a second time, though it cannot change. **Fix:** the semaphore is now taken per attempt (`for attempt ... : async with sem:`); an attempt that will be retried records its wait in `_retry_wait` and the sleep happens after the slot is released. A new pure helper `_is_permanent_client_error` is True for an `httpx.HTTPStatusError` with a 4xx code other than 408, 425 and 429; those fail at once with the same error row as before. 5xx, 429, timeouts and connect / read errors keep their one retry, and a recovering retry returns the normal row. The circuit-open lane (E416), the unexpected-error lane, the error row text and the dead-code "Max retries exceeded" tail (now after the loop) are unchanged. Tests: `test_e463_retry_pause_outside_scan_slot_round442.py` (new; slot free during the pause, a second symbol gets the slot between the first symbol's two attempts, 4xx not retried, 408/425/429/5xx retried, helper table). Not run here (no pytest/httpx in this sandbox); the existing `test_main_analyze_symbol.py` retry tests (503, ReadTimeout, ConnectError, MAX_RETRIES=0, shadowed range) should pass unchanged.

## 11 Nov 2026 - Round 441 (E462): a warm-cache hit no longer overwrites a newer stored price

 * **Round 441 (E462):** item 5 of the round 440 list (looked at in round 437, left because the cache has a TTL). On a warm hit `run_bulk_yahoo_price_feed_cached` pushed every served quote into the feed store. The cache is only rewritten by whole runs, while `patch_feed_price` and the live feed write single symbols in between, so a quote up to 120 s old (6 h when the market is closed) replaced a newer `last_price` / `current_price`. **Fix (data_feed.py):** with the per-quote write time from E461, each served symbol is compared with its stored row; if the row has a usable price and its `price_refreshed_at` is more than one second later than the quote's write time, the quote is not pushed (the symbol still counts as served, and the reply gains `kept_newer_feed_price`, the number of such symbols). A quote that is newer (or equal within the second) is pushed as before, and its row now carries `price_refreshed_at` = the QUOTE's write time instead of keeping the old stamp, so later comparisons are honest. Unknown times on either side (no stamp on the row, an unreadable stamp, no quote time) push as before. New pure helpers `_iso_epoch` (aware, naive = IST, trailing Z = UTC, junk = None) and `_row_price_is_newer_than_quote`. A failing row read is swallowed per symbol as the merge already was. Tests: `test_e462_warm_hit_newer_feed_price_wins.py` (new, 14 cases). Run here in the pinned-requirements venv: full api-gateway suite.

## 11 Nov 2026 - Round 440 (E461): the bulk quote cache merges, with a time per quote

 * **Round 440 (E461):** item 1 of the round 439 list. `set_bulk_quote_cache` replaced the whole shared map with the rows of the run that wrote it and stamped ONE timestamp on it. A run over a few symbols (a retry, a repair, a small request) therefore dropped every other cached quote, and the map then looked warm for the full TTL, so the next whole-universe request was answered from a cache holding a handful of names. **Fix (data_feed.py):** (1) every quote has its own write time in `_meta.quote_ts`; (2) the write MERGES into the stored map: this run's rows win, stored quotes older than the current TTL (120 s open, 6 h closed) are dropped so the map cannot go stale for ever, and a merge with nothing new writes nothing (it would only move the timestamp); `merge=False` is the old replace; (3) `_meta.full_run_ts` is the time of the last write that covered the whole universe; `run_bulk_yahoo_price_feed_cached` passes `complete=not symbols`, so only a run without a symbol list moves it; (4) a warm hit now serves a requested symbol only while ITS quote is inside the TTL, and a whole-universe request is a hit only while `full_run_ts` is (partial writes no longer stand in for it); (5) new pure helpers `bulk_quote_age_sec`, `bulk_full_run_age_sec`, `_as_ts`. A stored map from before E461 has no `quote_ts` / `full_run_ts`: its quotes count as written at its `_meta.timestamp` and the map counts as a whole-universe write, so nothing changes until the first new write; a map with no timestamp at all is still passed by the map-level gate as before. `_meta` gains `written`, `quote_ts`, `full_run_ts`; `count` is now the size of the merged map; the `/api/quotes/bulk-cache` route shows them with no change. Rows themselves are untouched (no key added to a quote, so nothing leaks into the feed store). Tests: `test_e461_bulk_quote_cache_merge.py` (new, 15 cases). Run here in the pinned-requirements venv: full api-gateway suite.

## 11 Nov 2026 - Round 439 (E460): a real flat day writes day_change_pct 0

 * **Round 439 (E460):** item 1 of the round 438 list. `merge_feed_payload` refused any incoming `day_change_pct` of 0 when a non-zero value was stored (the sparse-fallback guard it shares with volume / pe / roce / rsi), so a stock that genuinely closed flat kept yesterday's change in the feed (and in the scanners and Hot Picks that read it). The guard cannot tell a quote with no data from a real 0 by the number alone, but the row can: new pure `_flat_day_is_real(row)` is True only when the incoming row carries a usable `previous_close` AND a current price (`last_price`, `current_price`, `ltp`, `price` or `cmp`, first usable one) within 0.005% of it (the precision of the stored 2-decimal percentage). Only then is the 0 written. A bare 0, a 0 with only one of the two, an unusable previous close (0, negative, None, text, NaN, inf) and a one-paisa move on a cheap stock stay protected, and the other zero-protected fields (volume, pe_ratio, market_cap, roce, rsi) are unchanged. Writers already send the pair: the bhavcopy rows (close and previous close) and the market-data bulk quotes. Tests: `test_e460_flat_day_change_is_written.py` (new, 20 cases). Run here in the pinned-requirements venv: full api-gateway suite.

Health Audit unchanged: a flagged seed still counts as filled, `seeded_count` still reports it.  * **Round 427 (E447):** the last three unaudited feed-write routes: `start-bulk-feed`, `refill-additional`, `structure-refresh`. **Defect 1, `start-bulk-feed` had no double-start guard.** It never looked at the job row, so a double click (or the UI's retry) started two bulk workers on the same job row, and each call cleared the shared stop flag first, which wiped a Stop the user had just pressed. **Defect 2, `refill-additional`'s guard could never fire.** It answered `already_running` only when the job was running and `force` was false, but `force` defaults to true and `frontend/src/api.ts` always sends `force=true`; and the job row was only written after the awaits that resolve the symbols, so two requests could both pass. **Fix:** new `gateway_support/feed_start_guard.py`, used by both routes. A start answers `already_running` (HTTP 200, with the running job's fields) while a feed job made progress in the last 600 s (`BULK_FEED_STALE_AFTER_SEC`, floor 30) or Refill Additional's own mirror says running; a process-local claim covers the time spent resolving symbols and is released in a `finally`. A row with no or an unparseable `updated_at`, or one silent past the window, counts as stalled and can always be restarted; an unreadable job row fails open. The two routes and the slow-field `/data-feed/run` share one job row, so a bulk start while Refill Additional runs (and the reverse) is refused too. A refused start no longer clears the stop flag. `force` is still accepted but no longer overrides a live job (Stop it first); `start-bulk-feed` now defaults `force` to false. **Defect 3, the bulk worker ignored the run's verdict.** `run_bulk_yahoo_price_feed` returns `status` "stopped" (Stop pressed) or "error" (httpx missing), but the worker always wrote the job as "done" and stamped `last_success_at`, so a stopped or failed run looked like a finished one. It now keeps "stopped" / "error" and stamps the last-success meta only when the run did not fail. **`structure-refresh`:** the start path was already single-flight (lock plus job claimed before the response). **Defect 4, a Stop during planning was lost:** planning runs on the worker thread and `run()` clears the stop flag when it begins, so a Stop pressed during planning was lost and the full refresh ran anyway; a stale Stop left by an earlier run could also cancel nothing but looked set. The flag is now cleared when the run is claimed and checked after planning, which ends the job as `stopped`. Tests: `test_e447_feed_start_guard_round427.py` (24); `test_main_feed_control_audit.py` had two pins updated (running + force=true now refuses; an unreadable job row no longer turns into a 500, a failing job write still does).
 * **Round 426 (E446):** Refill All and Repair Batch. `POST /repair-all` now claims the job before it responds, so a double click or the UI's retry cannot start two jobs; the claim also resets the previous run's counters and cancel flag. Refill All's job and `repair-batch` audit with `cache=False` instead of the 20 s memo. Tests: `test_e446_repair_all_claim_round426.py`.

Defect: the release was unconditional. The foreground fundamentals refresh takes the lock for 5 s but its upstream call can run 35 s (kept on purpose in round 402), so the lock expired mid-call, a second request took it, and the first one's `finally: release_refresh_lock` then freed the second request's lock, so a third refresh could start while the second was still running (same for the 45 s background lock after a long outage). Fix (`data_feed.py`): new `acquire_refresh_lock(redis, symbol, ttl_sec)` returns an owner token (or `None` when somebody else holds the lock); the token is the Redis value (was `"1"`) and is kept in `_MEM_LOCK_TOKENS`; `release_refresh_lock(redis, symbol, token=None)` frees the process lock and deletes the Redis key only while the token is still the holder's (Redis: read, compare, delete; a read or delete error is swallowed and the TTL ends the lock). `try_refresh_lock` is unchanged for callers (bool, now a wrapper). **No change in `main.py` or its tests:** the token is remembered in a `ContextVar`, so `release_refresh_lock(_redis, symbol)` called in the task that took the lock, or in a task created from it afterwards (the fire-and-forget `_background_refresh_fundamental`, created by `asyncio.create_task`, which copies the context), releases only its own lock; `token=` can also be passed explicitly. A release from a context that never acquired (no token anywhere) keeps the old unconditional behaviour, so an unexpected call path degrades to what it did before. A refused Redis lock now also drops the owner entry it had just written. Not changed: the 5 s foreground TTL itself (so a second request can still start a refresh of the same symbol while the first runs past 5 s; that is the round 402 trade-off, a longer foreground lock would hold concurrent requests for up to 35 s), and the process lock is still left set after a Redis refusal. Redis read-compare-delete is not atomic (a Lua `EVAL` would be, but the Upstash client use here is `set` / `ttl` / `delete` only); the window is the gap between the read and the delete. (3) the repair route clears a stale `rsi_seed` when it stores a real RSI (local history and technical branches), otherwise the copied row's old flag would have made the merge treat the real value as a seed.

Run `test_data_feed.py` and `test_main_patch_single_stock_feed.py` on the VM.

(2) `bulk_yahoo_download_prices` placeholders (`source: yahoo_missing`) overwrite the row's `source` and stamp `price_refreshed_at = now` on a row whose price was not refreshed (nothing reads that stamp for freshness; labelling only). ## 11 Nov 2026 - Round 379: the intraday quote refresh no longer overwrites a feed row's prev_close with the live price (E390)

 * **Audit:** read `api-gateway/data_feed.py` (normalize / extract / merge helpers, `DataFeedStore` get / put / replace_fields / bulk read-write, `find_prepare_to_buy_candidates`, `patch_feed_price`, the bhavcopy feeder's row shape) and `instant_scanner`'s use of `prev_close`. Rest of the file (Yahoo bulk download, caches, price alerts) and the rest of gateway `main.py` / routers still NOT audited.
 * **Defect (`patch_feed_price`):** it wrote the live price into `price`, `close`, `cmp`, `ltp`, `last_price`, `current_price`. `put_symbol` then runs `normalize_feed_payload`, which renames `price` / `close` / `cmp` to `prev_close` (the last stored close, which `instant_scanner` compares the live price with: `change_pct`, `price >= prev_close`, the EMA fallback). So every intraday patch (`refresh_prepare_to_buy`) replaced the stored close with the intraday price. Reproduced against the real store: a row with `prev_close` 1000 read 1050 after `patch_feed_price(..., 1050)`.
 * **Fix:** `patch_feed_price` writes only `last_price`, `current_price` and `price_refreshed_at` (both price keys survive normalize and `_payload_price` still resolves them), works on a copy of the row, and leaves `prev_close` alone. Behaviour for bad / over-cap prices and for a missing row is unchanged.
 * **Tests:** `test_e390_patch_feed_price_keeps_prev_close.py` (prev_close survives two patches, readers still get the live price, the fetched row is not mutated). The existing `TestPatchFeedPrice` assertions (keeps other fields, `last_price` / `current_price` set, row created when missing) were re-checked by hand: pytest is not installed here, so run `test_data_feed.py` on the VM.
 * **Looked at, not changed:** (1) `normalize_feed_payload` maps `price` / `close` / `cmp` / `prev_close` onto one key, so a single write carrying both a live price and an explicit `prev_close` keeps whichever comes last in the dict (order dependent); no current writer does this after E390. (2) `day_change_pct` is zero-protected in `merge_feed_payload`, so a genuinely flat day (0.0%) keeps yesterday's non-zero value; the protection exists for sparse fallbacks that send 0, so it needs a decision. (3) `_payload_is_useful` tests `close` / `price` / `ltp`, which never exist on a normalized row, so a row with only price fields (no fundamentals) is never served from the local cache and is re-read from Neon each time (performance only). (4) `put_symbol` / `replace_fields` do not refresh the local legacy-key cache entry that the bulk write does (harmless: reads try the other keys first).

## 11 Nov 2026 - Round 365: position-stocks available_capital is capped at the pool ceiling while positions are open (E371)

 * **Found:** `available_capital` is a running ledger (reserve subtracts, release adds) that `sync_from_broker` only re-bases when the pool is flat. A release applied twice, one credited for a position that never reserved, or a pool that shrank could leave it above what the pool can spend while positions stayed open, and new entries were sized from money that was not there.
 * **Fix (`capital/available_guard.py`, `capital/ledger.py`):** while positions are open, `sync_from_broker` lowers `available_capital` to `total_allocated_capital - sum(capital_risked of OPEN / EXIT_LEGS_REJECTED)` when it sits above that by more than `SCALP_AVAILABLE_DRIFT_TOLERANCE_PCT` (default 5) % of the pool total, with a warning log. It only ever lowers. The full cost basis is read before the `SCALP_POOL_COMMITTED_MARGIN_FRAC` scaling. Switch `SCALP_AVAILABLE_CEILING_CLAMP` (default on, 0 = off), read per call. The flat-pool reset and the zero-drain reset are unchanged.
 * **Not covered (still open):** capital stuck LOW after a failed release is not repaired here: raising it needs a trustworthy figure for what is really free, and a wrong raise is the dangerous direction. The E366 queue (persisted failed releases) is what retries those.
 * **Why the bound is safe in normal flow:** the pool total adds back only the margin fraction of the open cost while the ledger takes off the full cost, so the running figure sits at or below the bound; only profit larger than the margin can lift it above, which the tolerance absorbs. Worked out by hand for the default fraction 0.20, not run against a live ledger.
 * **Tests:** `test_e371_available_capital_ceiling.py` (6: normal flow untouched and low never raised, drift lowered, tolerance, bad input, switch per call, wiring order). Run by hand here; the position-stocks suite was not run (no pytest or sqlalchemy installed). I checked by reading that the existing ledger tests that keep an open position with a set `available_capital` use values far below the ceiling, but did not run them.

## 11 Nov 2026 - Round 360: the failed-release queue and the watched unknown-state SELLs survive a restart (E366)

The in-memory queue stays the source of truth inside a process, so a failed save changes nothing.
 * **Known limit:** the save uses the same database that just failed, so an outage that blocks the release can block the save too; and a crash between a cover BUY being accepted and its row being deleted would, after restart, look at the SELL again (the guard reads the order book first, and a cover that already exists is joined, not doubled, only for the stop-driven path: the orphan path would send one more cover). The alert on reload tells the operator to check Dhan.

## 10 Nov 2026 - Round 356: a broker stop whose placement call failed without a clear refusal is looked up at Dhan and adopted, not placed twice (E359)

 * **Audited (`real-trade-service/execution/broker_stop.py`, `_place` and `sync_stops`):** the stop is booked as a `TradeOrder` row only after Dhan returns an order id. `cancel_for_exit` finds the stop through that row.
 * **Found:** if the placement call failed after Dhan had accepted the stop (timeout, dropped connection, or a reply with no order id), no row was written. The next sync pass saw no stop and placed a second one, and the first was invisible to `cancel_for_exit`, so a software SELL could leave a live SELL trigger order behind on a position that was already gone.
 * **Fix:** when the call went out and the error is not a clear refusal (RMS / EXCH / DH- codes, invalid IP, circuit band, eDIS, tick size, trigger-price relation), `_recover_unbooked_stop` reads Dhan's order book for an open SELL stop-type order on that symbol (or security id) and open quantity, tag BSTOP or empty, with an order id no `TradeOrder` row knows, and books it (`_adopt_stop`, with a Telegram alert). If the order book cannot be read, or the adoption commit fails, the symbol is flagged `_unverified`, backed off, and the next placement checks the book before sending anything. If the book is readable and holds no such stop, the failure was real and behaves as before. More than one unbooked match logs an ERROR and adopts the first. Clear refusals do not read the book.
 * **Tests:** `tests/test_e359_broker_stop_adopts_unbooked_order.py` (7 checks: lost response, reply without an id, unreadable book then later adoption, no stop at Dhan, clear refusal skips the book, matching rules, failed adoption commit). 6 fail on the round 355 file and pass now; the 7th (clear refusal) passes on both by design. Full `real-trade-service` suite run here: 6429 passed, 1 skipped. `check_shared_copies.py` and `check_merge_conflicts.py` are clean.
 * **Not verified live:** the field names read from Dhan's order book (`orderType`, `transactionType`, `quantity`, `tradingSymbol`, `securityId`, `correlationId`, `triggerPrice`) follow the names already used elsewhere in this service; check them against a real order book with one small position.

It goes through the same branch as CANCELLED: shares that did trade are booked first (and an EXPIRED row with filled shares but no usable price stays open to retry, as for the other dead statuses), a zero-fill SELL restores its position and counts the exit failure, a resting broker stop is not a failed exit. ## 10 Nov 2026 - Round 342: a REAL exit fill is booked in one commit and only then is the symbol lock released (E344)

 * **Audited (`real-trade-service/portfolio/portfolio.py`: `record_real_exit_sent`, `record_real_exit_fill`, `force_close_real_position`, `_open_positions_market_value`, `refresh_unrealized`, and the caller in `execution/reconcile.py`):** the P&L maths, the PARTIALLY_CLOSED / breakeven-stop handling, the cash credit, `refresh_unrealized` (it only writes equity, so it cannot overwrite a cash update) are sound. One defect, an ordering one.
 * **Found:** on a full exit, `record_real_exit_fill` (and `force_close_real_position`) called `shared_symbol_lock.release()` BEFORE the cash and P&L were booked. `release()` commits when it deletes a row, and rolls back when it fails. So (1) its commit saved the closed position before the cash and today's P&L were booked, and a failure right after left a closed position with no money booked (the daily-loss check then undercounts); and (2) if the release itself failed, its rollback undid the not-yet-committed close (qty back, status back) while the booking that followed still went through: the account was credited, the position was back to its old size, and the next reconcile pass booked the same fill again. Both need a database error at that moment; the failure is silent.
 * **Fix:** the release moved to after the one `db.commit()` that now holds the position, the cash and the P&L together (also in `force_close_real_position`). A failure in the booking commits nothing and releases nothing (reconcile retries the fill as before); a release that rolls back now has nothing of the exit left to undo. Partial exits still keep the lock. No other behaviour changed.
 * **Looked at, not changed (`entry_engine/entry.py`, two places):** the placement-failure branch (line ~2343) and `expire_stale_orders` (~2756) also call `release()` while an uncommitted `order.status = REJECTED / EXPIRED` is pending, so a failing release would roll that status back. The expiry case heals itself (the order is still stale next cycle, so it is expired again); the placement-failure case could leave the rejected order as PENDING. Fixing it means committing in the middle of the entry loop, which I did not do without the real suite; it is on the remaining list.
 * **Tests:** `tests/test_e344_exit_booking_before_lock_release.py` (5 cases; the real functions are pulled out of the source, so they ran here without sqlalchemy; 4 fail on the round 341 file, including the one that reproduces the rollback). The existing `test_record_real_exit_fill_full_close_releases_symbol_lock` and `test_refunds_cash_and_zero_pnl` read the same result and should still pass (real pytest not run here).
 * **Effect to expect:** none while the database answers.

 * **Audited (`real-trade-service/risk_engine/portfolio_heat.py`, `execution/heat_state.py`, `execution/shared_heat.py`, `execution/shared_order_budget.py`, `execution/shared_exposure.py`, and in `portfolio/portfolio.py` the account row, daily reset, `held_exposure_positions`, `record_real_fill`):** the heat maths (stop risk, gap allowance, sector surcharge, the shared cap), the order-budget conditional UPDATE and its fail-closed refusal, the peer exposure read and the in-flight BUY count are sound.  * **Found (audit item 6, read from the code, not measured):** one cycle needs 2 to 4 distinct chains and market-data spaces them 3.2 s apart (`DHAN_OPTIONCHAIN_MIN_INTERVAL_S`), so a cycle can take 6 to 13 s. The entry analysis fetched its chains BEFORE the stop checks, so the stops waited behind them. The Overview page fetched a chain per open position on every poll through the same limiter. A fetch that failed or timed out (client timeout 12 s) left the position with "no premium": the software stop was blind for that cycle.
 * **Fix (`fno/engine.py`):** `_get_chain` = one fetch per (underlying, expiry) per cycle, shared by the entry analysis, the expiry-day chain and `manage_open`. The chains of OPEN positions are fetched first. For open positions a fetch that raises is a missing chain (the entry analysis still lets a provider failure show as a failed cycle, `last_tick.ok = False`, as before).
 * **Fallback:** the engine remembers the last chain per key. A position whose fresh chain cannot be had is managed on the last one seen if it is at most `EXIT_CHAIN_FALLBACK_S` (30 s) old (journal kind `stale_chain`); older than that it is the old "no premium" path. `squareoff_all` uses it too. A constant, no new env name.
 * **Overview (`main.py`):** `GET /fno/overview` takes the engine's own chain when it is at most 10 s old (`Engine.recent_chain`) and only fetches when there is none.
 * **Tests:** `test_round295_chain_budget.py` (6; 4 fail on the round 294 code): open positions first, once per cycle, recent fallback, old chain not used, a raising fetch is not an aborted cycle, the age limit. `test_round294_exit_safety.py`: the two "one position raises" tests now raise from `_exit` (a raising provider is a missing chain since this round).

## 10 Nov 2026 - Round 294: an exit never waits for the entry locks; a part-filled stop is booked once; no SELL beside a stop whose cancel has not landed

 * **Found (audit of the round 293 CI-fixes zip):** (1) `_exit` used `real_allowed`, so a readiness blocker (a reconcile difference is one), a disarm or a mismatch left a REAL position open through its stop and the 15:15 square-off; `POST /fno/squareoff` answered `{"closed": []}` with no reason, and `/fno/disarm` also dropped the borrowed token and broker. (2) A broker-side stop that part-filled and then showed CANCELLED / EXPIRED was not booked and a new stop for the FULL quantity was placed. (3) `_sl_state` read the stop once after the cancel; a cancel still in transit read PENDING with nothing filled and the SELL went out beside the live stop (two sells = a short). (4) `DhanBroker.place` read the error body of an HTTP error inside the handler: a cut-short 5xx body raised `IncompleteRead` past `maybe_sent` / `exit_doubt`, so the next cycle could sell again. (5) One position raising (or a `build_order` ValueError) aborted `manage_open` / `squareoff_all` for every other position, every cycle.
 * **Fix 1:** new `execution.exit_allowed(cfg, broker)`: a broker with credentials is all that closing a held position needs. `real_allowed` still gates every BUY. A leftover from an EARLIER day with no ARM today is sold only while Dhan's net position still shows it (Dhan squares INTRADAY off itself; a SELL on nothing opens a short). `/fno/disarm` keeps the borrowed credentials while REAL positions are open (new orders stay blocked) and says so. `POST /fno/squareoff` returns `still_open` and a note.
 * **Fix 2:** `_absorb_stop_fill` books what a stopped / cancelled stop sold, once (`sl_booked_qty` on the position, so reading the same order again cannot book the same lots twice - this also fixes a latent double booking in the old `_sl_state` path). All sold = the position is closed at the stop's price; part sold = a closed child row, the new stop covers what is left.
 * **Fix 3:** `_await_final` re-reads the cancelled stop (the same tries / wait as an entry) until it is TRADED / CANCELLED / REJECTED; still PENDING after that = `wait`, no SELL.
 * **Fix 4:** the error body read is guarded (`_NET_ERRORS`); the HTTP code alone then decides (5xx = maybe sent). An answer that is not a JSON object counts as `NO_ORDER_ID`.
 * **Fix 5:** `_manage_one` per position inside try / except (journal kind `position_error`); `squareoff_all` the same; `build_order` ValueError in `_exit` / `_enter` is noted, not raised.
 * **Changed old tests (they pinned the old behaviour):** `test_round236` blocked-exit test now blocks by missing credentials; `test_round248` unarmed leftover: not sold while Dhan's positions are unreadable, sold once Dhan shows it; `test_real_partial` unreadable-stop test now misses more reads than the retries.
 * **Tests:** `test_round294_exit_safety.py` (15; 12 fail on the round 293 code). **Not covered:** the `/fno/disarm` and `/fno/squareoff` route changes (no test client here; run `pytest` on the VM). **Still open:** a restart drops a borrowed token, so open REAL positions then have no broker until ARM is pressed again (the audit's items 6 to 11 are not part of this round).

## 10 Nov 2026 - Round 292: an order whose call failed is looked up at Dhan by its correlationId (exit SELL and, new, the broker-side stop)

 * **Found (the open item from rounds 282 / 286):** a STOP-LOSS order whose POST failed with a network error or HTTP 5xx was treated as a plain failure: the next cycle placed another stop. If the first one had in fact reached Dhan, two resting SELL stops sat on the same quantity; if both triggered, the second one opened a short. (Round 282 had closed this for the exit SELL, but only by waiting for Dhan's positions, which cannot tell a resting order from a held position.) Both cases needed one read-only question to Dhan: what became of the order with this correlationId.
 * **Dhan call:** `GET /v2/orders/external/{correlation-id}` (Dhan's order API page: "Retrieve the status of an order by correlation id"). New `Broker.order_by_correlation` / `DhanBroker.order_by_correlation`: an order found is parsed like `order_status`; HTTP 404 is state `NOT_FOUND`; everything else (network error, 5xx, 400 / 401 / 429, an answer without an `orderStatus`) is `None` = cannot tell, never read as "not there". The reply shape for a missing order is NOT verified against the live API, which is why only a plain 404 counts, and only after 2 minutes for a stop (`STOP_ABSENT_AFTER_S`: a delayed order may still land).
 * **Exit SELL (`_resolve_exit_doubt`):** before Dhan's positions are read, the order is looked up. Traded: booked at Dhan's real price (positions still showing it held no longer matter). Resting: wait, no second SELL. Rejected / cancelled with nothing filled: the mark is cleared and the engine sells on the next cycle. Partial: the sold lots are booked like any partial exit. Not found / cannot tell / a mark without an id: unchanged (the round 282 positions rule). A 404 never clears an exit mark by itself.
 * **Stop orders (new):** every stop now carries our own correlationId (`sl...`). A failed call that `maybe_sent` (the round 282 classifier) stores `sl_doubt` + the time on the position and places no second stop. Each cycle the stop is looked up: found (resting or already traded) = kept as the position's stop (`sl`), no second one; rejected / cancelled with nothing filled, or 404 after 2 minutes = a new stop is placed; cannot tell = nothing placed. A plain 4xx refusal is NOT in doubt and retries exactly as before. An EXIT is never held back by a stop in doubt (that would leave the position unprotected): the lookup is tried first, and if it still cannot answer the exit goes ahead and the log says to cancel any stop for the contract in the Dhan app afterwards.
 * **Clear by hand:** `POST /fno/stop-doubt/clear?position=ID` (admin session) lifts the stop mark when you looked in the Dhan app and no stop is there; it places nothing. `GET /fno/overview` carries `stop_doubt` per open position.
 * **Frontend:** F&O > Overview: an amber "STOP IN DOUBT" chip, the explanation with the correlationId, the button "I checked Dhan: no stop is there, clear the mark" (asks for confirmation), and "N stop in doubt" on the State card. The round 289 exit-doubt view is unchanged and independent.
 * **Tests:** `test_round292_correlation_lookup.py` (18): the Dhan call (GET path, quoting, 404 vs everything else, list reply, blank id, base broker); exit SELL traded / resting / rejected / cannot-tell / no id; stop remembered with its id, no second stop while the lookup cannot answer, found stop adopted, rejected stop re-placed, 404 trusted only after 2 minutes, 4xx unchanged, exit not held back, clear by hand. 14 of the 18 fail on the round 291 code (the other 4 pin unchanged behaviour). Run here with a stand-in runner (no pytest / fastapi here): 18 of 18, and the existing engine tests that it can run (round 282, 283, real_partial, engine_paper, round 277 / 281) give the same results as before the change. Frontend: asserts at the end of `fnoView.test.mjs`; every `npm test` node test passes. NOT run here: the full F&O suite under real pytest, `tsc` / `vite build`.
 * **Needs one live check (the endpoint is from Dhan's docs, not yet seen answering):** after the next live probe, ask Dhan for one of its own orders by correlationId (the probe prints it) and compare with what Dhan shows; also what a made-up id answers (404 expected). Until then a not-found answer simply leaves things as they were.

## 10 Nov 2026 - Round 282: an exit SELL whose call failed is never repeated until Dhan's positions say what happened

 * **Found (audit of `probecheck.py`, `capital_board.py`, the `main.py` routes and the broker's failure handling; `probecheck` and `capital_board` read clean apart from a cosmetic point below):** round 277 made the engine log "the order may have reached Dhan" after a failed call and compare positions, but it still treated the failed exit SELL as a plain failure. (1) After a failed SELL the engine put the resting stop back and left the position OPEN, so the next cycle sent a second SELL: if the first had reached Dhan and both filled, the second opened a short. The re-armed stop had the same risk. (2) Only `status == "NETWORK"` counted as "may have reached Dhan". An HTTP 500 / 502 / 504 / 408 on POST /orders (a gateway can time out after Dhan's order system took the order) and a 2xx answer with no order id were reported as clear refusals ("Nothing is open" in the probe, no flag in the engine).
 * **Fix:** `execution.maybe_sent(result)` is the one test (network failure, HTTP 5xx or 408, or a 2xx without an order id and without error text; a 4xx such as DH-905 / DH-906 stays a clear refusal). `DhanBroker.place` reports a 2xx without order id and error text as `NO_ORDER_ID`. The engine, on a failed exit SELL of that kind, marks the position (`exit_doubt` with the correlationId, the reason and the limit price sent), puts no stop back and sends no second SELL. Each cycle, before anything else, `_resolve_exit_doubt` reads Dhan's net positions: flat -> the SELL went through, the position is booked as sold at the limit price sent (flagged in the note, check the contract note); the quantity still shown -> it may be resting, so still no second SELL and a journal line saying so; positions unreadable -> wait. `POST /fno/exit-doubt/clear?position=<id>` (admin) clears the mark after you looked in the Dhan app and the SELL is not there; it never places an order and is logged. The entry BUY and the probe (BUY and SELL) use the same test. `/fno/overview` open positions carry `exit_doubt` (true/false); `fnoApi.exitDoubtClear` is added, no button yet.
 * **Not changed:** a failed SELL that is a clear refusal (4xx) still puts the stop back and is retried next cycle; a plain rejection in the probe is still retried a little lower. The stop order's own network failure (`_place_sl`) is still only logged ("software stop only"): a stop that did reach Dhan but whose id we never got is not cancelled before an exit (see the remaining items).
 * **Cosmetic, not changed:** `probecheck.load` and `GET /fno/probe?file=` treat an empty `file` as invalid although the field comment says blank = newest; the UI never sends one.

 * **Found (audit of `realprobe.py`, with `readiness.py` read clean):** the manual probe (`scripts/fno_real_order_probe.py`) had the same blind spot round 277 fixed in the engine. (1) A BUY call that failed on the network (timeout, cut response) was reported as "Dhan REFUSED the BUY ... Nothing is open", exit code 2, although Dhan may have accepted it: a live 1-lot position could sit there while the tool said it was flat. (2) A SELL call that failed on the network was treated like a rejection and the loop sent another SELL on top of it; if both had been live and filled, the second would have opened a short.

A `NETWORK` failure on a SELL does the same, naming the contract and quantity to close by hand, and sends no further order. A plain rejection of the BUY (still exit 2, "Nothing is open") and of a SELL (still retried a little lower) behave as before.
 * **Not changed:** nothing is sent by this round; the probe stays a manual tool outside the engine's locks.
 * **Tests:** `test_round281_probe_network.py` (4; 2 fail on the round 280 code, 2 guard the unchanged rejection paths). F&O suite: 432 passed, 1 skipped here. No restart needed unless you run the probe from the container.

## 10 Nov 2026 - Round 279: an index that fails to analyse no longer stops the exits

 * **Found (audit of `engine.tick`, with `gates`, `sizing`, `paper`, `costs`, `store`, `expiry` read clean):** the per-index analysis (expiry, chain, candles, signals) ran inside the same `try` as everything else and BEFORE `manage_open`. Any exception there (an odd candle shape, a bad chain, a provider bug) aborted the whole cycle, so open positions were not checked: no software stop, no 15:15 square-off, no carried-over close, and the cycle failed again the same way every minute. Reproduced: a DEMO position left OPEN at 15:20 while the intraday feed raised.
 * **Fix:** each index is analysed in its own `try`. A failure is logged, recorded as a `strategy_error` event ("analysis of NIFTY raised ...: no entry from it this cycle, open positions are still managed"), shown as `analysis failed` in that index's decision, and that index is left out of this cycle's entries. The other index is analysed and can still enter, `manage_open` and the REAL reconcile always run, and the tick is still reported `ok: false` with the error, as before.

 * **Why:** the Overview "Pipeline check" was a flat list of facts.  * **Backend (`fno/stages.py`, new; `main.py`):** `build` is pure: it reads the engine's last cycle summary and today's journal events (signal, veto, skip, entry, exit, real_blocked, order_failed, stale; newest 500 per kind) and changes nothing the engine does. `GET /fno/pipeline` keeps `steps` and `locks` exactly as before and adds `stages` and `stage_summary`; if building the stages fails the route still answers with `stages: []`. Rules: market data PROBLEM names what is missing; chains PROBLEM on a failed or stale (over 90 s) cycle or an index with no chain; a gate block is the gates working (OK, never PROBLEM); no capital is a sizing PROBLEM until a later entry; a failed BUY or a REAL BUY held back by closed locks is an order PROBLEM; a failed stop / SELL, a held-back REAL SELL, or an open position with no premium is an exits PROBLEM until an exit comes after it; reconcile is REAL only and a difference with Dhan is a PROBLEM. Idle is never counted as OK; events from earlier days do not count.
 * **Frontend:** `FnoStagesRow` above the flat checks: eight boxes with the status in words, age and count today; a click opens the last decision and its full journal entry. ## 9 Nov 2026 - Round 260: a rolling backtest with no usable India VIX can no longer look good (VIX data-quality gate)

 * **Why:** the live engine refuses to trade while India VIX is unknown (`gates.entry_gates`: "India VIX unknown"). `rolling_sim.run` passed `vix_known if vix_known else 15.0` to the same gate, so with no `--vix` file (or a file that stops early) the VIX limit (`FNO_VIX_MAX`, 25) never blocked a day: the volatile days, which usually hurt a long-premium strategy, were all traded. Nothing in the result or the verdict said so.
 * **Fix (`backtest/rolling_sim.py`, `backtest/report.py`):** every tested day whose last VIX close BEFORE the day is missing, or older than `VIX_STALE_DAYS` (5 calendar days; a weekend or a long weekend fits) is counted. `data_quality` gains `vix_unknown_days` and `vix_unknown_pct`; above `MAX_VIX_UNKNOWN_PCT` (10 %) `ok` is false and the verdict is forced to `NOT_PROVEN` with the reason first ("... pass --vix with a daily close for the whole range"). The text report's `data quality:` line prints the VIX count; a note says how many days had none. The decision itself is unchanged (a missing value is still read as 15), so a run with a complete VIX file gives the same trades as before.
 * **Effect:** a run that passed no VIX file is now `NOT_PROVEN` / `NOT OK` whatever its P&L. `scripts/fno_rolling_backtest.py --vix vix.csv` (daily close, date + close) is now needed for a verdict. Results written before this round have no `vix_unknown_*`; re-run them.

## 9 Nov 2026 - Round 259: `fno_rolling_fetch.py --resume` also EXTENDS a series (a later `--to` or earlier `--from` fetches only the missing days)

 * **Why:** the files will be topped up as time passes (a new week each Friday) and the range pushed back once the backtest wants more history. Round 257's `--resume` refused any file made for another range, so every top-up meant the whole series again (about 80 calls per series per six months).
 * **Fix (`scripts/fno_rolling_fetch.py`):** a file of the same underlying / type / strike / interval / expiry / span but another range is now reused. `plan_extension()` makes the file cover the UNION of what it holds and what is asked for, so a gap between the two is fetched too (a hole never hides inside a range the file claims); only the missing ranges are fetched, merged with the held rows (each timestamp once), and `from` / `to` in the file become the union. A file that already covers the request is skipped. If the extension fails in part, the result is a `.partial` that already holds the old rows plus the progress; the complete file is left alone, and the next `--resume` prefers that wider partial and asks only for its failed windows (not the extension again). Another span, strike or interval is still never reused. Without `--resume` nothing changes.
 * **Tests:** `test_round259.py` (4; all fail on the round 258 code): the union / gap plan; a later `--to` makes only the new calls and gives one clean 10-day series; an earlier `--from` is added in front; a failed extension keeps the old file, and the next resume continues it. `test_round257` changed in one assertion (another range is now accepted). 49 passed in the stand-in runner (no pytest here); **run the full F&O suite on the VM.**

## 9 Nov 2026 - Round 258: a rolling backtest on too few strikes can no longer look good (data-quality gate on the held strike)

 * **Why:** the sim enters on the ATM contract of the moment and then holds that strike, finding its later candles among the fetched labels. With only `--strikes ATM` fetched, the held strike is in the file only while it is still the ATM; on every other bar there is no candle, the bar is "unmanaged" (no stop, no target is checked) and the trade is closed at the square-off. That removes the losing paths, so the result flatters the strategy. It was counted in `unmanaged_bars` and a note, but the verdict ignored it.
 * **Fix (`backtest/rolling_sim.py`, `backtest/report.py`):** the result carries `data_quality` (`held_bars`, `unmanaged_bars`, `unmanaged_pct`, `unpriced_exit_pct`, the strike `labels` fetched, `ok`). If more than 5 % of held bars had no candle for the held strike, or more than 10 % of exits had to use the last known price, the verdict is forced to `NOT_PROVEN` with the reason first ("fetch more strikes: ATM+-1, +-2"). The text report prints a `data quality:` line (OK / NOT OK). `RollingBook` records the labels. Limits are `MAX_UNMANAGED_PCT` / `MAX_UNPRICED_PCT` at the top of the file.
 * **Effect:** results written before this round have no `data_quality`; re-run them. A run on a complete ATM,+-1,+-2 fetch is unchanged.
 * **Tests:** `test_round258.py` (3; all fail on the round 257 code): enough strikes is OK and printed; a book where two bars in three have no candle is NOT_PROVEN and "NOT OK"; the gate itself via the limit. `test_round246` still passes. **Run with the stand-in runner only (no pytest here); run the full F&O suite on the VM.**

## 9 Nov 2026 - Round 257: `fno_rolling_fetch.py --resume` finishes a run that ended with failed windows (only those windows are asked again)

 * **Why:** a six-month run is about 80 calls per series and 4 to 20 series. One 5xx that outlasts the retries made the series a `.partial`, and the only way forward was to fetch the whole series again (hundreds of calls, and the same chance of another hole).
 * **Fix (`scripts/fno_rolling_fetch.py`):** new `--resume`. For each series: a complete file made for the same underlying / type / strike / interval / expiry / range / span is skipped; a `.partial` of the same series is loaded, only its `failed_windows` are asked again (`fetch_series(..., only=)`), the rows are merged with the ones already held (each timestamp once), and the result is written as complete when nothing failed again (the old `.partial` is then removed) or stays `.partial` with the windows that failed again. A file made for another range, span, strike or interval, or an unreadable one, is never reused: the whole series is fetched and the reason is printed. Without `--resume` nothing changes.
 * **Tests:** `test_round257.py` (4): refetch asks one call, not the whole week, and completes the series; a window that fails again stays listed; complete file skipped / other range, span, strike, interval refused / unreadable file; CLI end to end (first run partial with 6 calls, `--resume` 2 calls and complete, a third run 0 calls). With 255 / 256 / 16 ones: 36 passed in the stand-in runner. **The full F&O suite was not run here (no pytest / network): run it on the VM.**
 * **Left as it was:** `--resume` does not refetch holes of a series made with an older `--to`; extend a range by fetching the new range into the same folder under a new name, or delete the file.

## 9 Nov 2026 - Round 250: the two items round 249 left open (order size vs slippage, expired DEMO leftover)

In practice this turns some 2-lot entries into 1-lot entries when the budget was exact, and nothing else. `sizing.lots_for` itself is unchanged (it just receives the price that is really paid).

If the expiry has not passed, or the provider has no candle for that day, or it fails, the old price (the entry premium) is kept, and a failing provider never stops the square-off. REAL is not touched: the broker decides there.
 * Not changed: the index close is used as the settlement value (a proxy: the real settlement is the exchange's average of the last 30 minutes of the index, so a contract very near the money can differ by a few points).

REAL still needs its four locks: if the engine is not armed that day the SELL is not sent and a `real_blocked` event says so. No new switch.

## 9 Nov 2026 - Round 246: intraday backtest on REAL premiums (rolling data into the SIM, plan item C1)

 * **New:** `backtest/rolling_sim.py`, `scripts/fno_rolling_backtest.py`, `cli.main_rolling`. It runs the same strategies, gates, sizing, stops, trail and costs as the Black-Scholes sim, but every premium is a recorded Dhan expired-option candle (files from `scripts/fno_rolling_fetch.py`). Result kind `ROLLING`, shown with its own reliability label.
 * **How a trade is priced:** the signal is taken at the close of bar i (history up to that bar, daily candles up to yesterday); the fill is the OPEN of bar i+1 in the ATM contract of that moment, plus the synthetic spread. The strike is then held and its later candles are found by strike among all fetched labels, because the ATM series moves with the spot. Fetch `ATM,ATM+1,ATM-1,ATM+2,ATM-2` at least; with only `ATM` a trade can rarely be followed.
 * **Honest handling of holes:** files with `complete: false` (a failed window, round 245) are refused unless `--allow-partial`; a bar with no candle for the held strike is not managed and counted in `unmanaged_bars`; a position that cannot be priced at the square-off is closed at its last known candle and counted in `unpriced_exits`; signals with no ATM candle are counted in `skipped_no_quote`. A high count means: fetch more strikes.
 * **Not verified on real data (needs your one-week fetch, A8):** that Dhan's timestamps are the START of each bar (assumed, like the index candles), which expiry code matches `min_days_to_expiry` (pass `--expiry-code`; the expiry date is not in the reply), and that the strike labels reach far enough. The spread is still synthetic: the data has no bid / ask.
 * Tests: fno 208 passed (6 new: uptrend CE only, fill at the next bar's open, no look-ahead on the premium data, unpriced exit counted, incomplete / one-sided / missing files refused, CLI end to end). check_control_catalog and check_shared_copies OK.

## 9 Nov 2026 - Round 245: audit of the rolling backtest and the calibration-runner service

 * **Audited:** `backtest/rolling.py`, `scripts/fno_rolling_fetch.py`, and the whole runner service (`runner.py`, `jobs.py`, `scheduler.py`, `main.py`, `autocalib.py`). Held up: the lock / worker-pool logic (`_conflict`, `_pick`, memory reserve), the cancel and process-group kill, the `.part` -> final output file swap, secret redaction, the autocalib rules (loosening needs two different runs, protected keys, cool-down, steps) and the route auth (every route except /health is behind the admin dependency).
 * **Fix 1, rolling fetch: a failed run destroyed good data (real bug).** The fetch script wrote its file even when windows had failed: a 429 or timeout left a hole that looked like a complete series, and an expired token (every call 401) overwrote yesterday's good file with an empty one. Now: 429 / 5xx / network errors are retried with a doubling pause (a 401 is not retried); every file lists `failed_windows`, `empty_windows` and `complete`; a series with a failed window is saved as `<name>.json.partial` and never replaces the complete file; a series with no candles at all writes nothing; writes are atomic; a candle at a window edge is kept once. A backtest on these files must refuse a series with `complete: false`.
 * **Fix 2, rolling parser / request:** one unreadable timestamp raised and lost the whole 30-day window (now just that row is skipped); a zero or NaN close is dropped (a premium of 0 would break sizing); a non-list `timestamp` returns no rows; the strike label is checked (`ATM`, `ATM+1` .. `ATM+10`, `ATM-1` .. `ATM-10`) instead of reaching Dhan as an error. Bad `--from` / `--to` / `--strikes` stop the script with exit 2.
 * **Fix 3, runner: a full disk killed a worker thread for good.** `_save` inside the failure handler of the run loop could raise, which ended the thread; the page still counted it as a slot, so capacity shrank silently. The save and the after-run hook are now guarded. The same disk-full case in the scheduler raised after the slot was marked as fired, so the pack was never submitted and nothing said so; now it is still submitted, and a tick that fails is logged.
 * **Fix 4, runner: a crashed F&O backtest showed as green.** The wait steps of `fno_backtests` only knew "not running any more", so a simulation that ended `failed` inside fno-options-service gave a success. They now give `attention` (and the pack's Telegram) when the job that was started in this run ended `failed`; an old failed job from a skipped replay is not blamed (`fresh_key`).
 * **Fix 5, runner: parameters.** `float` parameters (stop %, target %, charges %, setup replay cost %) were never typed or bounded: a cost of -5, a stop of 0 or `nan` went onto the script's command line. They are now checked against their min / max like the integer ones; integers reject 3.7 and `inf` (was a silent 3 and a 500). `RUNNER_HEAVY_TIMEOUT_S=inf` crashed the import of the whole service; it now falls back to 6 h.
 * **Fix 6, runner: smaller ones.** A `meta.json` that is valid JSON but not a run (`[]`, `null`, no id) stopped the service from starting; it is skipped. The log tail cut a multi-byte character (rupee sign, arrow) at every 256 KB edge and its offset ran ahead, so the page lost text; it now cuts at a character boundary. The two zip downloads left a temp file in /tmp on every click; they are removed after sending. A file removed while a run is listed or zipped is no longer a 500.
 * **Autocalib:** `CAPITAL_ALLOC_MODE` is now in PROTECTED (like `CAPITAL_LEND_MODE`): no report may move the capital split from shadow to live.
 * **fno-options-service:** backtest job ids repeated when two jobs of the same kind started in the same second and the new record overwrote the old one; the id now carries a counter.
 * Tests: fno 202 passed (7 new, 1 skipped as root); calibration-runner 300 passed, none skipped (15 new; fastapi was installed here, so the 5 route tests that were skipped before ran too). The new tests fail on the round 244 code (checked: 15 of 15 and 7 of 7). check_control_catalog and check_shared_copies OK.
 * Not audited yet: nothing on the F&O list; the next audit item is "rolling (real premium) data into the SIM" (C1).

## 8 Nov 2026 - Round 231: F&O REAL path: partial fills, orders in doubt, unknown-origin positions (fno-options-service)

 * **Why:** round 230 never read `filled_qty`. A half-filled BUY that was then cancelled left Dhan holding lots we had no position or stop for; an exit SELL "in doubt" could be sent twice (an oversold short); a position of unknown origin could get a SELL / stop on nothing (a naked short).
 * **Entry:** a partial fill keeps the filled WHOLE lots at the real average price with a stop for exactly that quantity (less than one lot: no position, loud event); the cancel not landing flags it UNKNOWN.
 * **Exit / stop:** a partial SELL or a part-filled broker stop books the sold lots as a CLOSED child row (`parent_id`; not counted as a second trade) and keeps the rest OPEN with a fresh stop. A SELL whose state is in doubt is never repeated: the next cycle resolves it first.
 * **UNKNOWN entries:** no stop and never sold by the engine; each cycle they are settled from the order's own state (TRADED confirmed / REJECTED-CANCELLED closed as NOT_FILLED) or Dhan's net position (>= our qty = confirmed). A zero net position alone never closes one.
 * **`Broker.can_confirm`:** True for `DhanBroker` (a missing answer = network miss = retry / in doubt); False for the base class and old fakes (old behaviour unchanged).
 * **Tests:** fno 133 (was 92): 14 partial / doubt tests, 27 strategy / backtest tests. Repo guard `check_market_data_url_default` now lists fno-options-service (it was missing).
 * **Still UNVERIFIED against Dhan** (unchanged): `STOP_LOSS` payload, `GET/DELETE /orders/{id}` and `GET /positions` field names, and now also how Dhan reports `filledQty` / `averageTradedPrice` on a part-filled or cancelled order.

## 8 Nov 2026 - Round 230: F&O REAL path: fill confirmation, broker-side stop-loss, reconcile (fno-options-service)

 * **Why:** the REAL path recorded fills at the limit price and relied on a software stop only. A real fill price, a stop that survives a service crash, and a cross-check with Dhan are the minimum before any REAL day.
 * **Entry:** after the BUY the engine waits up to ~5 s for the order status; TRADED -> the real average price sets entry, stop and target; REJECTED / not filled -> cancelled, no position; state unknown after a cancel -> kept as a position, flagged `UNKNOWN`, and a `reconcile` event is written. Then a resting SELL `STOP_LOSS` order is placed at Dhan.
 * **Exit:** the resting stop is cancelled first (if it had already traded, the position is closed at that fill and nothing is sold twice); the SELL is confirmed the same way; an unfilled SELL is cancelled, the position stays OPEN and the stop is re-placed. A stop that vanished is re-placed each cycle. The software stop stays as the backstop.
 * **Reconcile:** `GET /fno/reconcile` (and every minute in REAL mode): our open REAL positions vs Dhan's net F&O positions. Differences are logged and shown on the Overview, never traded on.
 * **Compatible:** a broker that cannot answer status / cancel / positions (and DEMO) behaves exactly as before.
 * **Tests:** fno 92 (was 85): entry fill, unfilled entry, stop traded, exit order (cancel then sell), unfilled exit, reconcile, Dhan response parsing.
 * **Still UNVERIFIED against Dhan:** `STOP_LOSS` / `triggerPrice` payload, `GET/DELETE /orders/{id}`, `GET /positions` field names. This was written without network access and the REAL path has never touched Dhan. A 1-lot, far-from-the-money test with the engine in REAL, REAL_ENABLED on and a hand ARM is the next step (and the static IP must be whitelisted).

## 6 Nov 2026 - Round 222: a previous close on the wrong price scale (split / bonus / demerger day) no longer becomes a "-80 % day" (market-data, real-trade, position-stocks)

 * **Why (6 Nov log, audit of the round 221 zip):** KMEW arrived with open / high / low / ltp 641.0 / 647.9 / 606.0 / 608.3 and a previous close of 3143.3, so every reader saw -80.6 %. position-stocks caught it by luck (`_day_stats_plausible` threw the whole frame away), real-trade's `_quote_return_pct` had no check and the stock was only rejected because it was a loser. The cause is in the data, not in KMEW: the exchange feeds carry the RAW last close, and after a corporate action the day's prices are already on the new scale. Any ranking by day move (top mover, short candidate) could have listed it.
 * **Fix at the source (market-data `dhan_data/prev_close_guard.py`, generic, no symbol list):** (A) the circuit band is set around the exchange's own adjusted reference, so base = (upper + lower) / 2; a previous close more than 5 % from that base is replaced by it (`prev_close_flag: corrected`). (B) with no usable band, a stock whose open / high / low / price all sit more than 25 % on the same side of the previous close never traded near it, so the previous close is withdrawn (`prev_close_flag: suspect`, previous_close and day_change_pct null, never guessed). The raw value is kept in `previous_close_raw`. Idempotent, never raises, `PREV_CLOSE_GUARD_MODE=off` turns it off.
 * **Self-check (fail open):** if more than 5 % of at least 100 distinct symbols come out flagged in a day, the feed layout is wrong and not the data: the guard passes everything through for 15 minutes and logs one ERROR (`PREV_CLOSE_GUARD_TRIP_PCT / _MIN / _S`).
 * **Wired into every quote path:** Dhan rows (`dhan_data/quotes.map_item`), `_pad_quote_response` (all other sources, including the live-feed and AngelOne bulk rows; AngelOne bulk now passes `open`), the AngelOne single quote and the AngelOne movers sweep (a withdrawn row is not a mover).
 * **real-trade:** both candidate tracks skip a flagged quote with a clear reason (`reject_kind: prev_close_flag`) before any history call, because the daily history (ATR, 20-day high, 6-month return) is on the old scale that day too. `CANDIDATE_PREV_CLOSE_FLAG_REJECT=0` turns it off.
 * **position-stocks:** `_accept_day_stats` keeps open / high / low and withdraws only the previous close when everything else in the exchange frame agrees with the price (counter `ws_status()['day_stats_prev_dropped']`); a garbled frame (several fields wrong) is still rejected as before.
 * **Tests:** market-data `test_round222_prev_close_guard.py` (23), position-stocks `test_round222_day_stats_prev_close.py` (4), real-trade `test_round222_prev_close_flag_reject.py` (5).
 * **Not done here (from the 6 Nov audit):** Hugging Face 402 (needs credits or disable), dead RSS feeds, the `regime: strong` vs "weak market" wording and the dynamic_universe `.NS` churn (both unverified, not traced).
 * **Deploy:** rebuild `market-data-service`, `real-trade-service`, `position-stocks-service`. After a corporate-action day look for `dhan quote <SYMBOL>: previous close corrected` and `/status` counters `prev_close_corrected / prev_close_suspect`.
