## 4 Nov 2026 - Round 217: Real Trade may use the part of Position Stocks' half that sits idle (real-trade)

 * **Why (4 Nov log):** JSWENERGY was refused although Rs 9,038 was free in the Dhan account, because Real Trade could spend only a fixed 50 % of the free cash (`equity_sync`) and hold at most 50 % of the account's total (`capital_share_cap` in the risk engine), while Position Stocks used only Rs 2,599 of its Rs 9,611 half. Idle money, in the direction your sizing wants (use the idle money).
 * **Fix (`CAPITAL_LEND_MODE`, default `live`):** new pure module `execution/capital_lend.py`. total = Dhan free cash + Real Trade exposure + Position Stocks exposure; the peer's idle allowance = its share of the total minus what it actually holds; `CAPITAL_LEND_RESERVE_FRAC` (default 0.5) of that idle allowance stays free for it, the rest is lent. Two places use it: (1) `execution/equity_sync.py` - spendable cash = max(the old 50 % of free cash, free cash minus the reserve), never above the free cash; (2) `risk_engine/engine.py` `capital_share_cap` - the exposure cap = the fixed share + the lent part, never below the fixed share.

 * **Profit lock (`PROFIT_LOCK_MODE`, default `live`):** once the best gain reaches `PROFIT_LOCK_MIN_GAIN_PCT` (0.8 %), the stop trails the BEST price by max(0.35 %, `PROFIT_LOCK_RANGE_MULT` (3) x the stock's own average 1-minute range %), capped at 1.5 %; 0.6 % when there are no bars. Never below entry + 0.1 %, never loosened, at least two ticks better than the old stop, always under the live price (position event `PROFIT_LOCK`). It falls through to the target and ATR trail, which still run; REAL's broker stop follows `current_stop`.

## 4 Nov 2026 - Round 208: a write-behind batch that times out says so (and is counted), instead of logging "failed"

 * **Question from your 4 Nov log:** `write-behind batch of 1 audit row(s) failed (DatabaseError: ... DPY-4024: call timeout of 8000 ms exceeded`. Is the audit row lost? **No.** `write_behind.drain_once` recognises `DPY-4024` / "call timeout", puts the rows back at the head of the queue with their try count unchanged and opens the shared 20 s back-off (`WRITE_BEHIND_BACKOFF_S`); only a non-timeout failure counts a try and is dropped after three. The WARNING simply used the same "failed" wording for both cases.
 * **Change (`write_behind.py`):** a timed-out batch now logs `write-behind: DB call timed out writing N <kind> row(s) - the rows were kept and are retried after the 20 s back-off (Q row(s) queued; K timeout(s) since the last line ...)`, at most once per 60 s. A real failure keeps the old "failed" line. New counter `requeued_timeout` in `GET /write-behind/status` (rows put back after a timeout; `dropped_failed` and `dropped_full` are unchanged and still the only ways a row is lost).
 * **Not changed:** the 1.6-4.6 s single-row inserts in the log are the Oracle link itself (they run on the worker, not on a trade); a queue that stays full during a long outage still drops the OLDEST row (`dropped_full`), as documented.

I could not confirm NSE's exact parameter names from the repo or the web, so I did not guess; the NIFTY 500 board and the AngelOne sweep in the same log still produced 148 movers each, so the candidate list is not starved. ## 4 Nov 2026 - Round 186: the real Dhan entry fill is read right after the BUY (issue #6), so the stop and target follow it in 1-3 s instead of 10-13 s

 * **Checked first:** the 4 Nov log items for HMAAGRO and POKARNA entries ("no entry price" on the super-order row). It stops at once on a rejected / cancelled entry; a part fill is left to the reconcile loop; it never raises, and if nothing is found in time the reconcile loop corrects it as before.

## 4 Nov 2026 - Round 185: /check now rotates through all subscribed symbols, and the surprise scan reads the bulk-quote cache once per scan instead of once per symbol

 * **Checked first:** the 4 Nov 03:50-04:05 UTC log (8398 lines, 0 ERROR, 24 WARNING, 3576 HTTP 200). Two problems were confirmed in the code, not only in the log lines.
 * **Fix 1 - `event/main.py::check_for_changes` (`GET /check`):** the log said "stopped after 242s at 73/462 symbols ... the rest are next pass", but every pass began at index 0 and nothing remembered where it stopped, so the same first ~73 symbols were re-diffed and the tail of the list was never checked (the 1 s stagger alone caps a pass at ~240 symbols even when every symbol is cached). The pass now starts at `check_cursor` (saved with the subscription state) and advances it by the symbols it really finished. A symbol that is already in the event cache needs no network call, so its 1 s stagger is skipped (the stagger protects Yahoo). The response keeps `checked` (= symbols done this pass) and adds `total`, `complete`, `next_cursor`. A cursor past the end (list shrank) wraps; a junk cursor reads as 0.
 * **Fix 2 - `api-gateway/surprise_scanner.py` + `data_feed.py`:** `scan()` called `get_cached_quote()` -> `get_bulk_quote_cache()` -> `kv_get()` once PER SYMBOL from the event loop. On a memory miss `kv_cache._guarded_read` waits up to `KV_LOOP_READ_TIMEOUT_S` (1.5 s) on the loop thread, which is the "event loop blocked for 3.3 s / 3.7 s" stack in the log; the scans took 34-38 s against the 20 s deadline, so real-trade-service was served a 258-383 s old result (and one fetch hit its 25 s ReadTimeout). `scan()` and `prime_bulk_ticks()` now read the shared map ONCE on a worker thread (`_load_cache_snapshot`, per-scan context variable like the other per-scan state) and `_tick_from_bulk_cache` looks symbols up in it with no kv read. `get_cached_quote(symbol, cache=None)` takes the map as an optional argument; with no argument it behaves exactly as before. A slow or failed read (cut at `SURPRISE_CACHE_SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT_S`, default 5) gives an empty map, the same answer a failed per-symbol read gave, and the bulk prefetch / single-quote path answers instead. A `data_feed` without `get_bulk_quote_cache` keeps the old per-symbol path.
 * **Not verified here - needs the VM:** the scan duration. The blocking is gone, so it should drop, but whether it gets under the 20 s deadline depends on the market-data `/quotes/bulk` time. Look for `surprise scan finished: ... in Xs` and for the absence of `event loop blocked` after the rebuild. If scans stay above 20 s, the next step is the chunked bulk prefetch, not this.

On the 384 labelled headlines in `tests/event_lite_data.py` its polarity matches the label 53 percent of the time: 153 headlines read as 0 (unknown) that carry a clear direction, 27 act (+1/-1) where the label says otherwise, and 12 of those have the OPPOSITE sign. The 12 are one pattern each: `usfda` is in its regulatory list, so "gets USFDA nod / approval / clearance" reads as -1 (a veto on good news), and "skips / omits dividend" reads +1 because of the word `dividend`.  * **Change - `event/event_feed.py`:** the old function is `_classify_legacy`; `classify` dispatches by `EVENT_FEED_CLASSIFIER`. **`shadow` (default): nothing changes, the keyword rules decide exactly as before; event_lite reads the same headline and agreement is counted.** `legacy`: keyword rules only. `assist`: keyword rules stand, with two safe changes - keyword 0 and event_lite sure (confidence 0.75 or more, `EVENT_FEED_LITE_FILL_CONF`) takes event_lite's sign; keyword +1/-1 and event_lite sure of the OPPOSITE sign (0.8 or more, `EVENT_FEED_LITE_VETO_CONF`) becomes 0 (no entry and no veto); it never flips a sign and never raises a strength by itself. `lite`: event_lite decides sign and type (below 0.5 confidence = 0). ## 4 Nov 2026 - Round 172: a tiny offline classifier (`event_lite.py`) replaces the dependency on an LLM API for event types and headline sentiment

 * **Problem:** headline sentiment relied on Hugging Face (HTTP 400 / paused / no key all meant a neutral 0.0, so `news_score` was exactly 50 and said nothing), the main `/analyze` path used a four-word keyword proxy, and the event service typed titles by plain substrings ("Segment update" = board meeting because of "egm", "Amount raised" = guidance because of "mou").
 * **Change 1 - `event_lite.py` (new, standard library only, about 500 lines, no network, no model files):** reads one headline and returns type (results, guidance, dividend, corporate_action, board_meeting, bulk_block, insider, regulatory, legal, management_change, rating_change, other, none), polarity -1/0/+1, strength, whether it is about the company, and a confidence. It handles the cases a word list gets wrong: cost words (higher fuel costs = bad, lower costs = good), "loss narrows" vs "loss widens", guidance cut / raise, a beat next to a miss, a dividend next to bad numbers, rating affirmed vs cut, order won vs lost, market-wrap lines, and common Hinglish. Classified events also carry `event_polarity` and `event_confidence` when event_lite is sure. Four new types appear in the summary (Regulator, Legal, Management, Rating); no consumer elsewhere reads them (checked: only results / bulk_block / insider are read downstream).

Honest note: the older sets were tuned on over earlier rounds. `BLIND_R172` (39 headlines written before this round's rule changes) scored 94.9 percent polarity before them; its two misses were then fixed with general rules (guidance cut, Hinglish cost words), so it is no longer fully blind. ## 3 Nov 2026 - Round 167: a leftover leg order that Dhan makes itself is cancelled before an exit is sent, and a Dhan-vs-app position mismatch now raises an alert (JYOTICNC, extra BUY 1)

 * **Your report (3 Nov):** the Dhan app showed an extra BUY of JYOTICNC that you did not place (you never trade by hand in the Dhan app). The Super Order 323261103320675 (SHORT 1, entry SELL 938.75 at 12:05:16) shows `STOP_LOSS_LEG` TRADED and `TARGET_LEG` CANCELLED, so the stop did fire.
 * **Cause (from the order book, not from the app log - the log query for 12:00-12:15 IST came back empty):** when a Super Order leg triggers, Dhan turns it into its own plain order (tag `VTT_SQROFF`, its own order id). That order was a BUY LIMIT that kept resting. The stop watchdog then saw the price past the stop and covered at market, and `close_position_now` / `_fire_flat_sell` only cancel the three Super Order legs, which does nothing to a leg that has already triggered. `_filled_bracket_exit_leg` only reacts once the leg is TRADED, and it was not yet. When the price came back to the limit, the leftover order filled, so Dhan was LONG 1 while the app believed the trade was closed.
 * **Change 1 - `orders/leg_child_guard.py` (new), called from `eod_squareoff._fire_flat_sell` right before the exit order:** for a Super Order position (no plain stop of its own, not a CNC carry), reads the order book and looks for orders on this security, on the exit side (BUY for a short, SELL for a long), created at or after the position opened, with a tag starting `VTT`. The app's own exit orders (tag `EOD_SQUAREOFF` etc.) are left to the existing retry logic. Outcomes: nothing found / book unreadable / switch off -> exit as before; all live ones cancelled and read back dead -> exit goes; one already filled the whole position -> NO exit (`PositionAlreadyFlat`); one filled in part -> NO exit now, the exit-retry backoff tries again; one cannot be cancelled -> the exit STILL goes (an uncovered position past its stop is the bigger risk) and a CRITICAL Telegram alert names the order. Every path that sends a flat exit goes through `_fire_flat_sell`, so stop-breach, stagnation, momentum, manual and EOD exits are all covered.
 * **Change 2 - `orders/residual_guard.py` (new), alert only, called from the fast loop in `main.py`:** at most once a minute, when this service traded any stock today, reads Dhan's positions once. For each INTRADAY row of a security traded today with net quantity not 0 and not equal to what the app holds (sum of its OPEN / EXIT_LEGS_REJECTED positions, + long / - short), the same mismatch must last 90 s before ONE critical alert per (security, Dhan net, expected). A security with an exit still settling (`*_PENDING_RECONCILE`, or closed in the last 2 minutes) is skipped. Dhan flat while the app is open is not alerted (stop fills are booked by reconcile). It never sends an order. This is the net that would have shown this case within about two minutes, whatever the cause.
 * **Switches (both on the Real Money Calibration page, live, shipped true):** `LEG_CHILD_GUARD` and `RESIDUAL_GUARD_ENABLED`; tuning: `RESIDUAL_GUARD_INTERVAL_S` 60, `RESIDUAL_GUARD_CONFIRM_S` 90. Both read at call time, so a toggle applies without a restart (`scripts/check_control_catalog.py`: ok).

(b) A stock that real-trade-service also holds INTRADAY on the same day can raise a false mismatch alert; it is only an alert. With `MOMENTUM_SCALEOUT=true`, a LONG Super Order trade of 4+ shares that reaches the momentum BOOK level before 14:30 IST is split: Dhan positions checked, TARGET then STOP leg cancelled and read back, MARKET SELL of half, then AT ONCE a plain SELL stop for the rest, then the row is rewritten (plain stop id, new stop, `flow_json["scaleout"]` stamp) and the half is booked through `overnight_stop.book_delta` (quantity, capital, P&L, ledger). A position is split at most once.
 * **Fallbacks:** nothing sold yet (cancel not confirmed, positions unreadable, SELL refused) -> the whole position is closed the old way. A leg already filled or Dhan showing fewer shares -> nothing is sent. Stop cannot be placed -> half booked, stray stop cancelled, rest sold at market. Half-sell not confirmed in `SCALEOUT_FILL_WAIT_S` -> booked later by the guard; no flat SELL is sent meanwhile (`settle_before_flat_sell`). Half-sell dies after acceptance -> stop cancelled, whole position sold.
 * **After the split:** `run_scaleout_guard` (main.py fast loop, after the plain-short guard) books the kept half's broker stop fill (STOP_HIT, total P&L includes the half), re-places a dead stop once then sells at market, exits at the target, and sells if the price sits under the stop `SCALEOUT_STOP_GRACE_S`. `eod_squareoff._fire_flat_sell` cancels and reads back the stop of a split position before any flat SELL, so a stop and a SELL can never both rest.
 * **Switches:** `MOMENTUM_SCALEOUT` (Controls page, default false), `MOMENTUM_SCALEOUT_MIN_QTY` 4, `MOMENTUM_SCALEOUT_UNTIL_IST` 14:30, `SCALEOUT_STOP_GAP_PCT` 1.0, `SCALEOUT_FILL_WAIT_S` 6, `SCALEOUT_STOP_GRACE_S` 15. Off = nothing changes.

The Dhan writer already split a timed-out chunk into two halves once, but a half that failed again, a chunk under 20 rows and the held-position chunk were lost the same way until the next poll.

Rows of a write that failed for good are sent ONCE more, `LIVE_QUOTES_RETRY_CHUNK` rows (default 10) per transaction: the Dhan writer right after the failed write in the same writer pass, the AngelOne writer when its queue is empty. A retry that fails is dropped, not queued again. A row is skipped when its symbol was written successfully (or has a newer row waiting) since the failure. Rows older than `LIVE_QUOTES_RETRY_MAX_AGE_S` (default 12 s; 0 = retry off) are dropped, because the table stamps `updated_at` with the time of the WRITE and an old price must not look fresh against real-trade-service's 20 s window. Counters are in `feed_status()["retry"]` and the Dhan live-store `status()["retry"]`.
 * **What it does NOT do:** while the shared Oracle back-off is open (after a DPY-4024 timeout, 20 s) only held-position rows are retried; the other rows wait and usually expire, because hammering a saturated database is what group347 / group356 stopped. So the retry mainly helps non-timeout failures (a dropped connection, a pool error) and the held-position rows; a real Oracle stall is still handled by the back-off, not by this.

Expected charges are logged for every candidate (`cost gate: qty ...`) and the WAIT text shows the weighting. Both are Real Money Calibration switches protected from autocalib.

## 3 Nov 2026 - Round 151: P0 memory round (Position Stocks tick budget, memory telemetry, no-copy helpers, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX, 2400m limit) and the half-sell probe stop fix (no change to entry / exit rules)

 * **Your request (3 Nov):** "start with priority round code fix" on the Full Plan v2 (merged), section 0.3 and section 5 P0. Position Stocks was killed at 09:34 and peaked at 900 MB at 10:51 (549 MB ten minutes before, 679 MB after the limit was raised).
 * **Change 1 (total tick budget, `WS_TICK_BUDGET`, default 1,500,000 ticks, about 160 MB at the measured 112 bytes per tick; 0 = off):** `feed/ws_client.py` checks the total every 5,000 ingests (at most every 10 s). Over the budget, symbols that no trade-decision caller has read in the last `WS_TICK_PROTECT_S` (900 s) keep one tick per `WS_TICK_THIN_S` (5 s), and up to 40 of the largest idle buffers are rewritten to that spacing per pass. The budget switches off again below 85% of itself. A symbol is "in use" when `get_tick_buffer()` was called for it outside the scan, so open positions, stops, breakeven, trailing, entry timing, excursion, event hook and every other reader keep full tick resolution. The all-symbol scan (`screening/engine.scan` and `scan_shorts`) runs inside `ws_client.bulk_scan()` (thread-local) so reading 2,600 buffers does not mark all of them in use. The newest tick always survives a rewrite. The per-symbol cap and the 65-minute age prune are unchanged.
 * **What this can change in trading:** the scan's 1 / 5 / 15 / 60 minute percent-change windows read idle symbols at 5-second resolution only while the box is over the budget. A symbol that becomes a candidate is read by the entry path and from then on is stored at full resolution (its older ticks stay thinned). Nothing else reads idle symbols. Set `WS_TICK_BUDGET=0` to get the old behaviour.
 * **Change 2 (telemetry):** `/ws-status` (`ticks`) and `/board/status` (`memory`) now show ticks buffered, symbols with ticks, estimated buffer MB, budget state, protected symbols, thinned skips and rewrites, ticks ingested, process RSS, peak RSS (`VmHWM`), threads and the cgroup usage and limit. The service logs one `position-stocks memory:` line a minute and warns once at 70% of the container limit.
 * **Change 3 (no buffer copies just to count):** `ws_client.tick_count(symbol)` and `ws_client.last_tick(symbol)` added. NOT wired into `screening/engine.py` lines 373 / 551 as the plan suggested: about 20 existing tests patch `ws_client.get_tick_buffer` with a stand-in and would see zero ticks through the new helpers. The scan still copies a buffer per symbol; the budget is what bounds the memory.
 * **Change 4 (compose):** `position-stocks-service` `mem_limit` 700m -> 2400m (your VM ran 1600m, then 2539 MiB by `docker update`), and `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2` (override with `PS_MALLOC_ARENA_MAX`). Compare `VmHWM` over one full session. After the deploy run `docker compose up -d position-stocks-service`.
 * **Change 5 (half-sell probe, no live order path):** (a) `place_intraday_sell_stop` retries ONCE as `STOP_LOSS` with a limit `SELL_STOP_LIMIT_BUFFER_PCT` (0.5%) under the trigger when Dhan answers "Trigger Price should be greater than Price" (the ONGC failure of 3 Nov); any other refusal still raises at once; the result carries `order_type_sent` and `limit_price`, and the probe prints which form Dhan accepted (Q4). This is a hypothesis about Dhan's rule, so the next probe run decides. (b) The probe refuses to start above `PROBE_MAX_MEMORY_PCT` (80) of the container limit. (c) Q5b records how long after the stop was in the SELL took to show as filled.
 * **Not changed, on purpose:** the stop is still placed right after the SELL is accepted, not after it fills (the plan asked to wait for the fill first): Dhan's message is a price rule, not a position rule, and waiting would lengthen the unprotected window the probe exists to measure. The fill wait is measured instead (Q5b).
 * **Read, no change:** JSWENERGY double BUY. `working_buy_symbols` (group297) already blocks a second BUY while the first is PLACED / PARTIAL, and an entry order is cancelled after `ENTRY_VALIDITY_MINUTES` (15). 09:17 + 15 minutes is before 09:40, so a second order after an expired first one is the expected path; whether the first one really filled needs the Dhan app / command A2b. BANKINDIA #268 overnight: no code path found that keeps a position when `OVERNIGHT_HOLD_ENABLED=false`; needs command A2c output.

## 1 Nov 2026 - E285 round 113: a positive news event type's weight follows what trades on that type did (position-stocks)

 * **Your request (1 Nov):** "do the next fix" (remaining item: learned event weights; round 106 recorded the typed event on every entry and reports follow-through per type). The feed's fixed weights (`TYPE_WEIGHT`: regulatory 0.9, results 0.85, deal 0.7, order 0.65, rating 0.45, management 0.4, other 0.2) are not changed and the feed service is not touched: the learned part is a multiplier Position Stocks puts on the strength it reads.
 * **New `orders/event_weights.py`:** from the closed, setup-stamped trades (`event_stats.summarize`), for each POSITIVE event type: learned multiplier = 1 + the type's average R clipped to +-0.5 (+0.3 R reads 1.3, -0.4 R reads 0.6), put through `adaptive_params.learned_value` with the constant 1.0: exactly 1.0 until the type has 30 closed trades with a readable R, then shrunk with `w = n / (n + 30)` (half weight at 30 trades) and held inside `EVENT_WEIGHT_MIN_MULT` 0.6 and `EVENT_WEIGHT_MAX_MULT` 1.2 (a hard bound). New strength = min(1, strength x multiplier). The age decay (one-hour half-life) is not changed.
 * **Negative events are never touched.** A negative event's strength drives the `NEG_EVENT` veto and the short setups, and learning must never weaken a veto; the multiplier is applied only when the polarity is +1.
 * **Where it is read (cache reads, no database, no I/O):** `screening/quality_gate._typed_event_from` (the event the entry's quality signal, the gap-against-event check and the setup stamp see) and `screening/premarket_plan` (the morning event candidates). Not changed: the stop-move hook for held positions (`orders/event_hook.py`, an exit), the feed itself and Real Trade's own event reader.
 * **How the cache is filled:** `slot_ladder._load` (the closed-trade rows the size ladder and the exits already read, at most every `SLOT_LADDER_CACHE_S` 300 s) calls `event_weights.update(rows)`, and `GET /setup/stats` refreshes it and now shows `event_weights` (each type's multiplier, source, trades, average R). So every multiplier is 1.0 in a fresh process until the first trade-reading call (the first entry, exit check or `/setup/stats` read).
 * **Switch:** `EVENT_WEIGHTS_LEARNED_ENABLED` (true; catalog "Entry guards", live; on the calibrator's protected list) and the round 110 master `ADAPTIVE_ENTRY_PARAMS` (help text updated). `EVENT_WEIGHT_MIN_MULT` / `_MAX_MULT` are in `.env.example`; `tests/conftest.py` turns it off for older tests.
 * **Side effects to know:** nothing changes on deploy: a type needs 30 closed trades with a readable R, and `/setup/stats` reads at most the last 1,000 settled positions still held, so at a few news entries a day that is weeks per type. After that a winning type can pass the strength floors more easily (up to x1.2) and a losing one less (down to x0.6). Selection feedback: a type whose strength is lowered gets fewer entries, so it learns more slowly; the shrinkage and the 0.6 floor keep it from being switched off by a few losses. The stamped strength is the adjusted one; the learner uses only type, polarity, age and R, so it does not feed on itself.
 * **Tests:** new `tests/test_e285_round113_event_weights.py` (7 tests, all pass; two deliberate breakages, negatives no longer protected and the quality-gate hook removed, each made them fail). The quality-gate function is exercised by itself (the module needs sqlalchemy / httpx, not installable here). `test_e272_premarket_plan`, `test_e273_slot_ladder` and the silent-excepts test give the same results with and without this round; `test_e285_round110_adaptive_master` has the same single failure as on the round 110 tree under my stand-in runner. Calibrator tests (19), `check_control_catalog`, `check_shared_copies`, `check_merge_conflicts` and `gen_env_reference` pass. **Not run:** the full position-stocks suite, and `slot_ladder._load` against a real database (VM).
 * **Honest limits:** only the strength is learned, not the half-life (the hour is the feed's and is unchanged), and only the up side. The R-to-weight rule (1 + average R, 0.6 to 1.2) and the 30-trade prior are my choices, not measured. Short-side (S4) and Real Trade entries are not stamped with their event yet (the short stamp is built where the quality signal is not in hand), so only long entries teach it.

**Deploy:** `bash scripts/vm_all.sh apply <zip> && bash scripts/vm_all.sh deploy` (position-stocks and calibration-runner). **VM check:** `bash scripts/docker_test.sh position-stocks-service tests/test_e285_round113_event_weights.py tests/test_e285_round106_event_stats.py tests/test_e272_premarket_plan.py tests/test_e273_slot_ladder.py tests/test_e285_round110_adaptive_master.py tests/test_group322_no_new_silent_excepts.py -q`, then `bash scripts/docker_test.sh calibration-runner-service -q`. **Watch:** `/setup/stats` -> `event_weights.types` (each type reads `source: constant` and multiplier 1.0 until it has 30 trades).

 * **Your request (1 Nov):** "do the next fix and give me updated zip" (plan item 10, per-stock adaptive values). First finding, as asked: the bar recorder (`feed/bar_recorder.py`) keeps 1-minute OPEN / HIGH / LOW / CLOSE / VOLUME per stock per day (45 days), so a stock's own one-minute RANGE and its own VOLUME PACE can be learned now.  * **New `orders/own_norms.py`:** for a symbol it reads the last `ENTRY_OWN_NORMS_DAYS` (20) recorded days before today, keeps only COMPLETE days (first bar by 09:20, 80 % of the 375 minutes, half of them with volume), and takes (a) the median one-minute range % over 09:45-15:15, then the median over days, and (b) the median over days of the cumulative volume traded by each minute of the session. Each is turned into the gate's number with `adaptive_params.learned_value`: the fixed constant itself until `ENTRY_OWN_NORMS_MIN_DAYS` (5) complete days, then shrunk toward it with `w = days / (days + 10)`, then held inside +-`ENTRY_OWN_NORMS_BAND` (50 %) of the constant (a hard bound). A symbol is a cache read: the first ask starts one background load and answers "unknown" (= the old constant); the pre-open warm-up (`screening/preopen.py`) queues the first 40 queued names so most entries already have norms. An empty recorder or failed read is cached as unknown for 30 minutes. Never raises, never waits, never does I/O on the entry path.

 * **Liquidity gate (`orders/liquidity_gate.py`):** the relative-volume test (and `rvol_ratio`, used for the size penalty) compares today's volume with the stock's own normal volume by this minute (shrunk toward and held within +-50 % of the old `20-day average volume x market-wide curve`) instead of the old figure alone. A nonsense own value falls back to the old base.
 * **Switch:** `ENTRY_OWN_NORMS_ENABLED` (true; catalog "Entry guards", live; added to the calibrator's protected list). `ENTRY_OWN_NORMS_DAYS`, `_MIN_DAYS`, `_BAND`, `_VWAP_RANGE_MULT` are in `.env.example`. Tests: new `tests/test_e285_round108_own_norms.py` (16 tests, all passing as a plain script); `tests/conftest.py` turns it off for older tests. `test_group333_vwap_gate.py`, `test_group333_liquidity_gate.py` and `test_group322_no_new_silent_excepts.py` pass under a stand-in runner. Not run here (no sqlalchemy / httpx, pip cannot reach them): the full position-stocks suite, including the entry tests that walk both gates. `docs/ENV_REFERENCE.txt` regenerated (1,797 variables); catalog, shared-copies and merge-conflict checks pass.
 * **Side effects to know:** this can LOOSEN a gate. A lively stock (median one-minute range 0.30 %) now tolerates up to about 0.2 % under the VWAP (was 0.15 %), and a stock whose own volume by this time is lower than the market curve is judged against its own lower pace, so it passes the relative-volume floor more easily. A quiet stock gets a TIGHTER VWAP tolerance (down to 0.075 %). The 50 % band and the 5-day minimum are the limits; set `ENTRY_OWN_NORMS_BAND` lower, or the switch false, to take it back.

The multiplier 1.0 and the 20-day window are my choices, not measured. The weekly 25 % limit is not applied (the value is a rolling 20-day median of the stock's own data, recomputed each day, not a stored learned value). ## 1 Nov 2026 - E285 round 107: the trail distance learns from how deep the setup's winners dipped before their next high (position-stocks, calibration-runner)

 * **Your request (1 Nov):** "do the next or all build?" - one round at a time, so this is the next item (plan item 11: the trail ignored the setup winners' giveback). Two findings changed the shape of it. (1) The 1-minute range the plan names is always smaller than the 5-minute range the trail already uses, so adding it can never change the distance (`max()` of the two): nothing was built for it. (2) A winner's plain giveback (best price minus exit price) is circular for a trail: a trade that exited on the trail gave back about the trail distance by construction. So the number that is learned is different: the deepest pullback from an in-profit peak that price then RECOVERED from (went on to a new high). That is the dip a winner of this setup normally survives; a trail closer than that shakes the next winner out.
 * **Recorded (every open trade):** `orders/excursion.py::recovered_dip_pct` reads the tick buffer since the open and `run_excursion_tracking` keeps `flow_json["peak"]["dip_pct"]` (raised, never lowered; a short mirrors it; a dip below entry before the trade is in profit is adverse excursion and is not counted; a pullback still going on at the end is not counted). `setup_stats.summarize` adds `dip_n` and `dip_p75_pct` (75th percentile over WINNERS, 10 samples minimum) to every cell, so `/setup/stats` and the calibration cells show them.
 * **Applied (only with proof):** new `orders/trail_dip.py`. For an open position on an explicit setup (never the legacy shortlist cell) whose cell has 30+ closed trades and 10+ winners with a recorded dip, the trail distance becomes `plan distance + w x max(0, learned - plan distance)`, learned = `dip_p75` held to +-25 % a week (`learned_limit`), `w = n / (n + 30)`. It only ever WIDENS the trail, and `exit_adaptive.trail_distance_pct` still caps it at the stop (`TRAIL_MAX_DIST_STOP_FRAC`). `trailing.py` passes the cell's dip into both the long and the short trail. Without a dip the distance is exactly what it was. Switch `TRAIL_LEARNED_DIP_ENABLED` (true; catalog "Exit and stop protection", live; added to the calibrator's protected list). New `tests/test_e285_round107_trail_dip.py` (18 tests, all passing as a plain script with stubs for sqlalchemy / models / dhan_client). Not run here (no pytest / sqlalchemy): `tests/test_trailing.py`, `tests/test_excursion.py`, `tests/test_e252_adaptive_exits.py` (they need sqlalchemy); `test_e272_setup_stamp_stats.py` (8) and `test_e275_learned_exit_numbers.py` pass under a stand-in runner; `test_e282_learned_stop.py` shows the same 3 failures with and without this round under the stand-in, so they are the stand-in's, not the change's. `docs/ENV_REFERENCE.txt` regenerated; catalog, shared-copies and merge-conflict checks pass.
 * **Honest limit:** nothing changes on deploy. Trades opened before this round have no `dip_pct`, so a cell needs 10 new winners with a recorded dip (and 30 closed trades) before any trail moves; at a few entries a day that is weeks. The dip is read from the in-memory tick buffer, so a dip older than the buffer is missed (the value only underestimates, which makes the trail less wide, not wider). Real Trade has no setup cells for this and is not changed.

**Deploy:** `bash scripts/vm_all.sh apply <zip> && bash scripts/vm_all.sh deploy` (position-stocks and calibration-runner). **VM check:** `bash scripts/docker_test.sh position-stocks-service tests/test_e285_round107_trail_dip.py tests/test_trailing.py tests/test_excursion.py tests/test_e252_adaptive_exits.py tests/test_e275_learned_exit_numbers.py tests/test_e282_learned_stop.py -q` and `bash scripts/docker_test.sh calibration-runner-service -q`. **Watch:** an open position's `flow_json` gets `"peak":{...,"dip_pct":x}` once it has been in profit and recovered a dip; `/setup/stats` cells show `dip_n` rising for winners.

## 1 Nov 2026 - E285 round 105: the event feed collector polls on the trading-day clock instead of one flat 5 minutes, and a fast poll is no longer answered from the 300 s cache (analysis-intelligence)

 * **Your request (1 Nov):** "do the next fix and give me updated zip and remaining item list" (plan item 5, event feed cadence). Real Trade's own news scan already ran on the new clock (E272 rounds 6 and 7: every 30 min from 15:30, every 2 h overnight, every 10 min from 08:00, every minute from 09:00, every 3 min from 09:20). The gap was upstream: `event/event_feed.py`'s collector, which that scan reads, polled its seven RSS sources every 300 s all day, so a 09:05 headline could reach Real Trade up to 5 minutes late however often Real Trade asked. The collector now follows the same clock (IST): `EVENT_FEED_EVENING_S` 1800 for 15:30-20:00, `EVENT_FEED_NIGHT_S` 7200 for 20:00-08:00, `EVENT_FEED_RAMP_S` 600 for 08:00-09:00, `EVENT_FEED_OPEN_S` 60 for 09:00-09:20, `EVENT_FEED_SESSION_S` 180 for 09:20-15:30. Every interval has a 60 s floor, the sleep is cut at the next boundary (the loop is awake at 08:00, 09:00, 09:20, 15:30 and 20:00), and Saturday and Sunday use the night interval all day (my choice; NSE holidays are not known to the collector, so they run the weekday clock). Pure functions `poll_plan(now)` and `next_delay_s(now)`; one log line `event feed cadence: <phase>, every N s` at each phase change. Switch `EVENT_FEED_CADENCE_V2` (1; 0 = the old flat `EVENT_FEED_POLL_S`, which is now used only then); restart the analysis-intelligence service to change it.
 * **A second cause, fixed:** the shared downloader (`news/feed_fetch.py`) keeps every parsed feed for 300 s (Google News searches 120 s), so a one-minute poll would have been answered from the cache four times out of five. `fetch_feed_ex` takes a new optional `max_age_s`: a GOOD cached copy older than that is not used and the feed is downloaded again. The collector passes 80 % of the current interval (48 s around the open, 144 s in session). A cached failure, empty or blocked answer is never bypassed, and the collector's own block cooldown (1800 s) still leaves a 403 source alone. Every other caller is unchanged (`max_age_s=None`).
 * **Side effects to know:** around the open the seven sources are downloaded up to once a minute (20 minutes a day) and every 3 minutes in session, against every 5 minutes before. The two Google News feeds are the likeliest to answer 429; the existing cooldown then leaves them alone for 30 minutes and the other five carry on. If `scripts/check_event_sources.py` or the log shows repeated cooldowns in the 09:00 window, raise `EVENT_FEED_OPEN_S` to 120.
 * **Tests:** new `tests/test_e285_round105_event_feed_cadence.py` (14 tests: phases and intervals, weekend, sleep cut at boundaries, a morning chain of wake-ups, env overrides and floor, the switch, `max_age_s` with a stubbed httpx / feedparser). Ran here as a plain script, all passing, together with `tests/test_e280_event_feed.py` (19). Not run here (no pytest / httpx / feedparser): `tests/test_feed_fetch_fallback.py`, `tests/test_event_main.py` and the rest of the analysis-intelligence suite. `docs/ENV_REFERENCE.txt` regenerated (1,791 variables); `check_control_catalog.py`, `check_shared_copies.py`, `check_merge_conflicts.py` pass.

Every Real Trade entry already carried a setup stamp (`flow_json["setup"]` on its ENTER decision: setup id, trigger, confirmations, size penalties, size multiplier, time slot), but no route sent it. `GET /positions/{mode}` and `GET /positions/{mode}/history` now add `setup` per row, joined from the ENTER decision made at or just before the position opened (the same join the entry-tape field already used; the open-positions poll skips the TAPE_TIGHTEN count so it stays two cheap queries at most), and each trade record of `GET /positions/{mode}/records` carries `setup` too. New `setup_stamp.public()` gives the shape the screens read (same keys as Position Stocks).
 * **On screen:** the Positions card has an `Entry reason` line (setup name and slot, hover for trigger, confirmations, penalties and size); a Trade History row shows `in: <setup> · <slot>` under its exit reason, and the opened row has an `Entry reason` line in its detail list; the history CSV gains `entry_setup` and `entry_slot` at the end. It reuses `entryReason()` from `setupView.ts`, so it reads exactly as in Position Stocks: an old trade shows `-` with "No setup stamp" in the hover text. Today every Real Trade entry reads "Shortlist (old rule)" with the shortlist label as its trigger, because Real Trade stamps the baseline unless a setup matched; the size penalties of rounds 99 to 103 (VIX, open cues, gap rank, opening window) show in the hover text.
 * **Honest limit:** a broker-imported holding and any trade opened before the stamp existed have no stamp, so they show `-` (never a guess). A trade whose ENTER decision was more than an hour before the position opened (a long-waiting limit order) will not match and shows `-` too.
 * **Also fixed (found by running the whole suite):** the round 102 `open_cues` handler in `entry_engine/entry.py` ended in a bare `pass`, which made `test_group322_no_new_silent_excepts` fail (4 found, 3 allowed). It now logs at debug level; the entry behaviour is unchanged (still fail-open).

**Deploy:** `bash scripts/vm_all.sh apply <zip> && bash scripts/vm_all.sh deploy`, then rebuild the frontend container. **VM check:** `bash scripts/docker_test.sh real-trade-service tests/test_e285_round104_entry_reason.py tests/test_group322_no_new_silent_excepts.py tests/test_e271_tape_history_and_stats.py -q`. **Watch:** Real Trade, Positions tab: each open card shows `Entry reason` (a bot entry reads `Shortlist (old rule)`; a demat holding reads `-`); Trade History tab: closed rows from now on show `in: ...`.

## 1 Nov 2026 - E285 round 103: the stock's own gap rank is computed, so the "gap above the 95th percentile of its own gaps halves the size" rule can fire (position-stocks, real-trade)

 * **Your request (1 Nov):** "do the next fix" (plan item 1: `gap_pctile` was never computed in either service, so the 95th-percentile half-size rule in `setup_engine` (`GAP_HALF_PCTILE`) was dead code). New `gap_rank.py` (identical in `position-stocks-service/orders` and `real-trade-service/entry_engine`, registered as an IDENTICAL family in `check_shared_copies.py`) keeps each stock's last 60 overnight gaps, `(open - previous close) / previous close`, from its daily bars (`structure_observation.fetch_daily_bars`, market-data `/history`, 120 calendar days). Today's own bar is dropped so a gap is never ranked against itself; a pair beyond +/-60 % (split / bad bar) is skipped. `pctile(symbol, gap_pct)` is a cache read (no I/O, never blocks) that returns where today's SIGNED gap ranks among those gaps, 0..1 (`adaptive_params.overnight_gaps` / `gap_pctile`, added identically to both copies of `adaptive_params.py`), and starts a background load for a symbol it has not seen. Both entry paths put it into the setup facts as `gap_pctile` (Real Trade `entry.py` before `classify_long`; Position Stocks `orders/entry.py` after the slot ladder; PS `setup_live.INPUT_KEYS` now lists it, Real Trade's already did); above 0.95 the setup size is halved by the existing rule. The 09:08 / 09:10 pre-open warm-up of both services also starts one background thread that loads the queued symbols' histories (up to `PREOPEN_WARM_MAX_SYMBOLS`, 40), so most entries already have a rank. A stock with fewer than `GAP_RANK_MIN_SESSIONS` (30) gaps, a failed fetch (retried after 30 min) or a history not loaded yet keeps the old size. Switch `GAP_RANK_ENABLED` (true; false = the rule stays off as before) in both control catalogs; `GAP_RANK_SESSIONS` and `GAP_RANK_MIN_SESSIONS` in `.env.example`. New `tests/test_e285_round103_gap_rank.py` in both services (12 tests each); both `conftest.py` files turn it off for older tests. Not run here (no pytest / httpx / sqlalchemy): the 24 new tests passed under a minimal stand-in runner with stubbed imports; the wiring in the two `entry.py` files was compiled but not exercised.
 * **Side effect to know:** only a gap UP above the 95th percentile of the stock's own signed gaps halves a size; a big gap DOWN ranks low and is left to the existing gap-down rules. The first entry on a stock whose history is still loading has no rank (the next cycle does).

**Deploy:** `bash scripts/vm_all.sh apply <zip> && bash scripts/vm_all.sh deploy`. **VM check:** `bash scripts/docker_test.sh real-trade-service tests/test_e285_round103_gap_rank.py -q` and `bash scripts/docker_test.sh position-stocks-service tests/test_e285_round103_gap_rank.py -q`. **Watch:** a setup entry log line `matched ..., sized x0.25` (or x0.50) on a stock with a large gap up; if every stock shows no rank, check that market-data `/history/<symbol>?period=6mo&interval=1d` answers.

## 1 Nov 2026 - E285 round 102: Real Trade reads overseas cues at 08:30 and sizes the morning's long entries down on a weak lead (real-trade)

 * **Your request (1 Nov):** "do the next fix" (plan item 4 of the remaining list: Real Trade did not read overseas cues in the morning; `global_cues` was used only for the carry decision at 15:00). New `entry_engine/open_cues.py` takes ONE reading of the cues that are live at 08:30 IST (`^N225`, `^HSI`, `ES=F`, `NQ=F` through market-data `GET /global-cues`; Europe is left out because at 08:30 its last bar is yesterday's close) and stores it for the IST day. Weak = the average day move is at or below `OPEN_CUES_WEAK_AVG_PCT` (-0.9 %) or a US-futures cue is at or below `OPEN_CUES_WEAK_US_FUT_PCT` (-1.2 %): every long entry is sized x`OPEN_CUES_WEAK_MUL` (0.7); twice as weak (-1.8 % / -2.4 %): x`OPEN_CUES_VERY_WEAK_MUL` (0.5). It rides in the existing soft-gate size penalties (`_soft_pen["open_cues"]`, floor `SOFT_GATE_FLOOR`), ends at `OPEN_CUES_UNTIL_IST` (10:30), never refuses an entry and never sizes up. Needs `GLOBAL_CUE_MIN_READINGS` (2) readings, else no opinion; an empty answer is asked again after 300 s; a failure never blocks anything. The read is started from the auto-pilot loop next to the 09:08 pre-open snapshot, and `GET /open-cues/status` shows the readings, level and the multiplier now in force. Switches `OPEN_CUES_ENABLED`, `OPEN_CUES_WEAK_MUL`, `OPEN_CUES_VERY_WEAK_MUL` in the control catalog; the rest are in `.env.example`. New `tests/test_e285_rt_open_cues.py` (16 tests); `tests/conftest.py` turns it off for older tests. Not run here (no pytest / httpx): the 16 new tests passed under a minimal stand-in runner with stubbed imports; the wiring in `entry.py` / `auto_pilot.py` was compiled but not exercised.
 * **Honest limit:** whether Yahoo answers for these four symbols from the VM at 08:30 could not be checked offline. If it does not, the log says `[open_cues] no overseas reading this time` and nothing changes.

**Deploy:** `bash scripts/vm_all.sh apply <zip> && bash scripts/vm_all.sh deploy`. **VM check:** `bash scripts/docker_test.sh real-trade-service tests/test_e285_rt_open_cues.py tests/test_e285_rt_results_split.py -q`. **Watch tomorrow at 08:30:** `curl localhost:<real-trade port>/open-cues/status` (readings filled?) and the log line `[open_cues] N reading(s): ...`; on a weak day the entry log shows `sized x0.70 by soft gates (open_cues x0.70)`.

## 1 Nov 2026 - E285 round 91: a swing take-profit level learned from the ledger, with the two columns it needs (real-trade)

**Your decision (1 Nov):** "do the swing target in the next fix". The open item said the ledger had no per-setup target data and that a rule and a column were needed. Both are added; the rule is inert until the ledger has the data, so **nothing changes on the day you deploy**.
 * **Columns (`trade_swing_ledger`, additive migration `db._ensure_swing_ledger_columns`, runs on boot like the others, Oracle `BINARY_DOUBLE`, Postgres `DOUBLE PRECISION`, both NULL):**
   - `peak_pct`: the best high the trade reached, in % over its entry price. Kept up to date at every evening scan for SHADOW rows (`engine.settle_shadow`, from the bar's high) and for OPEN LIVE rows (`live.after_scan`, from the scan row's high); never lowered (`lane.peak_pct_after`). Rows that closed before this deploy have no peak and are not counted.
   - `target_px`: the take-profit level a new LIVE entry gets when it is bought. NULL when nothing is learned yet. SHADOW rows never get one.
 * **Rule (`swing/learned_target.py`, mirror of `learned_hold.py`):** with 30+ CLOSED ledger trades that have a peak and 10+ winners (net > 0), learned % = the median of the winners' peaks; target % = max(learned %, `SWING_TARGET_MIN_R` (1.5) x the trade's own stop %, `SWING_TARGET_MIN_PCT` (3 %)); `target_px` = entry x (1 + target %). Under 30 trades or 10 winners there is no target. The ledger read is cached 10 minutes and fails to "no target".
 * **Where it acts (`live.eod_holds`, the 15:00 hold decision):** a position that `hold_verdict` would carry overnight, and whose price is at or above its `target_px`, is NOT carried: the normal square-off sells it ("target ... reached: profit taken at the close", logged as `SWING_EXIT_DECISION` and in the ledger note). It only ever turns a carry into a sale, before the carry cap. **No resting broker order, no stop change, the buy order is unchanged (`target_price=None`), no change to the SHADOW lane** (it keeps the no-target replay rules, so the numbers are not learned from their own effect). A target touched and given back inside the session is not caught (the stop and the 15:00 decision are the only watchers).
 * **Switches (Calibration tab, Swing lane, live, on the calibrator's protected list):** `SWING_LEARNED_TARGET_ENABLED` (ships `true`; OFF = no target is set and a stored one is ignored), `SWING_TARGET_MIN_R`, `SWING_TARGET_MIN_PCT`. `docs/ENV_REFERENCE.txt` regenerated; two new files added to `docs/FILE_MANIFEST.txt`.
 * **When it starts to matter:** the first targets need 30 closed trades WITH a peak, i.e. roughly the first month of evening scans after this deploy (the SHADOW lane closes several a week). Until then every swing position behaves exactly as in round 90. The 1.5 R / 3 % floors and the median are my choices, not yours or a replay's; they are the three switches above if you want them changed.
 * **Tests:** new `tests/test_e285_swing_target.py` (17: peak never lowers, target sale rules, learned value is the winners' median only, floors, cache and failure paths, the shadow lane records a peak and never a target, the order carries no target, the target applies only after `hold_verdict` says keep and before the cap, migration and switches present); `tests/test_db.py` lists `_ensure_swing_ledger_columns` in `COLUMN_FUNCS`, so its legacy-schema, idempotency and Oracle-type checks cover the new columns.
 * **Ran here (no pytest, SQLAlchemy or Docker in this sandbox; plain stand-in runner):** the 17 new tests; the 81 existing swing, learned-hold, event and catalog tests that import without a database (all pass, the one my runner cannot drive fails identically on the round 89 tree); `test_swing_lane.py` standalone; `test_autocalib` (19); `scripts/test_control_kit.py` (20); `check_control_catalog`, `check_shared_copies`, `gen_env_reference --check`, `check_merge_conflicts`; `py_compile` on every touched file. I also broke the rule two ways on purpose (median to p75, target turning a sale into a keep) and the new tests failed both times. **Not run:** the Real Trade pytest suite, `tests/test_db.py`, the new `live.py` paths against a real database (entries, `eod_holds`, `after_scan` are checked by source-order tests and the pure helpers only), Docker.
**Deploy:** `docker compose up -d --build real-trade-service`. On boot the log should show `added trade_swing_ledger.peak_pct` and `added trade_swing_ledger.target_px`. **VM check:** `bash scripts/docker_test.sh real-trade-service` (expect the old 5838 plus the 17 new and a few `test_db` cases). **After the first evening scan:** `SELECT symbol, status, peak_pct FROM trade_swing_ledger WHERE kind='SHADOW'` should show a peak on every OPEN row.

## 1 Nov 2026 - E284 round 83: the normal volume pace learned from the recorded bars (position-stocks)

**What:** the RVOL half of `ADAPTIVE_ENTRY_PARAMS` (plan E282 item 2). The liquidity gate's relative-volume test (`LIQUIDITY_RVOL`, and the size penalty built on it) compared today's volume with `normal daily volume x share of the session elapsed`, and that share was a guessed curve, `(minutes / 375) ** 0.6`. New `orders/volume_profile.py` measures it: for every COMPLETE recorded day (starts within 5 minutes of 09:15, 80 % of the minutes present, not backfilled, no index files) and symbol it takes the cumulative share of the day's volume by each minute, and the curve is the median over all of them (made non-decreasing). `liquidity_gate.elapsed_fraction` passes the old value through `volume_profile.adjust`.
**Guard rails:** needs 5+ complete recorded days AND 300+ symbol-days, else the old curve unchanged; shrunk toward the old curve with n / (n + 300); the result stays within +-25 % of the old curve at that minute (a hard bound) and never above 1; built once in a background thread and cached 6 hours, so the entry path never waits for the disk; any error, an unready build or the switch OFF gives the old value. `ENTRY_MIN_RVOL`, the 09:45 start and every other liquidity test are untouched. Switch `VOLUME_PROFILE_LEARNED_ENABLED` (ships on, inert until the data exists) in the Calibration tab under Entry guards and on the calibrator's protected list; `tests/conftest.py` turns it off for older tests.
**Limits:** the sample is the symbols the recorder keeps (top by turnover plus scan candidates), market-wide rather than per stock, and about 9 days at most today; the old curve front-loads about 22 % by 09:45, so the 25 % band is what decides how far this can move at first. Not built: a per-stock own-minute percentile, the VWAP-tolerance and spread percentiles.
**Tests:** `tests/test_e284_volume_profile.py` (7: straight curve from flat volume, too few days or symbol-days gives no curve, late or thin files excluded, shrink and the +-25 % band, off / not ready / broken gives the old value, the gate uses it, switch in config and catalog). Ran here with a plain stand-in runner: those 7, `test_e273_rvol_penalty` 4, `test_e37_catalog_coverage` 3, `test_group477_catalog_matches_config`, `test_e283_long_target` 13, calibration-runner `test_autocalib` 19, `check_control_catalog.py`, `check_shared_copies.py`, `gen_env_reference.py --check` (1,754 variables). **Did not run:** pytest and the Docker suites; `test_group333_liquidity_gate` imports pytest so it did not run here (its `elapsed_fraction` assertions are unchanged because the profile is off or empty in tests).

The existing `shared_order_budget` is a DAILY cap only. Every other order call (entry, cancel, exit, convert) is counted and NEVER delayed, so an exit or a protective stop does not wait behind a trailing move; counted calls use up the budget, so modifies yield to them. Fails open (any error = no wait). `ORDER_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` (live, ships on) and `ORDER_RATE_PER_S` in the Calibration tab under Entry guards; both on the calibrator's protected list; `docs/ENV_REFERENCE.txt` regenerated. `tests/conftest.py` turns the limiter off by default so older tests never sleep.

## 1 Nov 2026 - E282 round 76: a stop learned from the setup's own winners (position-stocks)

**What:** the first half of `ADAPTIVE_ENTRY_PARAMS` (plan E282 item 2, the item the plan rates highest). A stop used to depend only on the stock's own noise, the same for every setup. A setup's closed WINNERS record how far they went against the entry before paying (`min_price_seen` for a long, `max_price_seen` for a short). New `orders/learned_stop.py` takes the 90th percentile of that distance for the setup's cell, adds 10 %, holds it to +-25 % a week (`learned_limit`), shrinks it toward the plan's own stop with `n / (n + 30)`, and uses it as the stop. Long (S1 / S2 / S3) in `orders/entry.py`, short (S4 / S2 / S3) in `orders/short_entry.py`; the note is stamped in `flow_json["learned_stop"]` (record only; the short side through `short_live.py`).
**Guard rails (plan, "Guard rails for every learned value"):** a cell with fewer than 30 closed trades or fewer than 10 winners with a readable excursion gives the plan's stop unchanged; the stop only ever gets TIGHTER (never wider than the plan's), a long's rounded down to the tick and a short's up so the rounded stop is never tighter than computed; never below the stock's own noise floor (the largest of `LEARNED_STOP_MIN_PCT` 0.5 %, `OPENING_GATE_MIN_STOP_ATR_FRAC` x daily ATR and the E251 volatility floor), and with no daily ATR, or when that floor is on and cannot be read, the stop is left alone; the legacy shortlist cell never learns (it mixes long and short entries); the target, the 2:1 floor and the SIZE are untouched: the position is still sized from the plan's stop (`_budget_stop_pct`), so a tighter stop lowers the risk and never grows the position. The Time Machine and cost gates judge the levels AFTER this.
**Also:** `setup_stats.summarize` cells gain `mae_n` and `adverse_p90_pct` (winners only; None under 10 samples; a winner that never went against the entry counts as 0). Switches `LEARNED_STOP_ENABLED` (live, ships on: it does nothing until a cell has 30 trades) and `LEARNED_STOP_MIN_PCT` in the Calibration tab under Entry guards; both are on the calibrator's protected list (`autocalib.py`); `docs/ENV_REFERENCE.txt` regenerated.
**Expect:** most stops will not move at first. The E251 floor already puts many plan stops near the stock's noise, and a learned stop never goes below it. The note shows up on a trade only when the stop really was tightened.
**Tests:** `tests/test_e282_learned_stop.py` (28: winners-only excursion, 10-winner minimum, short reads the high, cell choice and fall-back to ALL, legacy never learns, short S2 own cell, shrinkage, weekly limit, tighter-only, tick rounding both ways, noise floor, configured minimum, unreadable floor fails closed, unknown ATR, switch off, wrong-side stop, short mirror, stamp, the wiring read as text: size from the plan stop, the setup known before the call, the Time Machine after it).
**Ran here (plain stand-in runner; `pytest`, `sqlalchemy` and `httpx` are not installable in the build sandbox):** the 28 new tests, `test_e37_catalog_coverage` 3, `test_e272_setup_stamp_stats` 8, `test_autocalib` 19, `test_regime_shadow_report` 8, `check_shared_copies.py`, `check_control_catalog.py`, `gen_env_reference.py --check`, byte-compile of every changed file: all pass. **Did not run:** the Docker suites, `tests/test_e274_short_target.py` and the other database-backed suites. The noise-floor test uses a stand-in for `orders/adaptive.stop_floor_pct` only when the real module cannot be imported (as in the build sandbox); on the VM it uses the real one. Five `test_e275_*` tests fail in the sandbox with or without this change (they need `sqlalchemy`).
**Not done:** the RVOL-percentile half of `ADAPTIVE_ENTRY_PARAMS`, a learned long target, the VWAP and spread percentiles; Real Trade is untouched (swing trades have no setup cell with closed-trade history yet).

## 1 Nov 2026 - E278 round 75: sweep study (offline script, no trading effect)

**What:** new `scripts/sweep_study.py` (+ `scripts/test_sweep_study.py`, 24 tests, wired into `.github/workflows/service-tests.yml` beside `ma_baseline`). It answers the one question the Liquidity Lab material leaves open: after a liquidity sweep, does price reverse, continue, or neither, on NSE data. It is an offline study like `ma_baseline.py` and `preopen_momentum_study.py`: it imports no service, reads no env, places nothing, adds no switch and no database column. Not a shadow mode.
**Direction-agnostic:** every event is scored as a long and as a short, with a day-clustered 90 % bootstrap (all stocks of a day share the market's move) and a matched baseline. A side counts as an edge only when BOTH intervals (net after costs, and excess over the baseline) are above zero. Fewer than 30 events per direction (or fewer than 20 day clusters) prints counts only: `insufficient_sample`, nothing else.
**Parts:** A daily (`sweep_low` / `sweep_high` = wick through the previous day's low / high by at least 0.10 ATR14 and a close back inside; `break_high` / `break_low` = a close beyond it, the second ICT bias rule). Entry = next open, exit = close of day i+h for h = 1 (the next session), 3, 5; cost 0.30 % + 0.10 % slippage; baseline = the same stock's non-event days of the same month; raw and market-adjusted views. B the full 3-step pattern on recorded 1-minute bars (daily bias, 30-minute sweep with rejection, 5-minute displacement of 1.5 x ATR and 60 % body within 3 bars, order block within 5 bars before it): COUNTS ONLY, never an edge verdict. C failed opening-range break (09:15-09:19 range; first closed break before 09:55; a close back inside within 3 bars = failed, otherwise held; returns to 10:00 / 10:30 / 15:00 at 0.15 % cost; baseline = held breaks).
**Pre-registered:** one sweep depth (first of `--depths`, default 0.10), one displacement size, one reclaim window, one primary horizon (h = 1; 10:00). Extra values are reported but never used for a verdict; every variant is counted in `variants_tried`.
**Not run here:** nothing on real data (no history folder or `bar-records` in the build sandbox, no network); the 24 tests use fixed synthetic bars and pass under the plain runner (`python3 scripts/test_sweep_study.py`). `pytest` is not installable here, so the CI line is untested.
**VM step:** `python3 scripts/fetch_history_for_backtest.py ...` (daily history for the 744-name swing universe, same loader as `ma_baseline.py`), copy the `bar-records` volume to the host, then `python3 scripts/sweep_study.py --daily HIST_DIR --bars BAR_DIR --out OUT_DIR`. Read the verdict per kind; the plan's table (section 4, E278) says what ships for each outcome. E279 to E281 are NOT built: they exist only if this study supports a direction.

# Stockky v2 - Changelog

One file for the whole history, newest first. Add **one bullet per release** at the top of the first list: `- E<number> (<date>): what changed and why, switches/env names,
tests that ran and tests that did not`. Do not create per-release `CHANGES_*.md` files or other Markdown notes: the repo keeps only `README.md` and this file.

Release notes, audit reports, service sheets and session notes that used to be separate files (about 790 `.md` files) were folded into this changelog on 2026-10-28
(E245) and removed from the working tree. File names quoted inside older entries refer to those removed files; they are in git history
(`git log --diff-filter=D --name-only -- "docs/*.md"`, then `git show <commit>^:docs/<file>.md`).

## Releases (E-numbered, newest first)

- **E274 round 44 (31 Oct 2026): setups S2 and S3 can match a short (position-stocks-service).** **Found:** `setup_engine` already knows S2 (weak stock of the day breaking its opening range) and S3 (exhaustion after a spike) for a short, but nothing fed it short facts, so `setup_short.decide` only ever looked at S4 and returned at once without a negative typed event. **Fixed:** `orders/setup_inputs.py` gets the short mirrors (`gather_short`, `s2_facts_short`, `s3_facts_short`, `pullback_hold_short`, `structure_ok_short`, `tape_exhaustion_short`, `wall_close_short`; `spike_z` takes an optional direction): range-low break or rally-back-and-fail, bearish candle, volume, up-spike beyond the stock's own volatility, shooting-star failure at the high, buying exhaustion / absorption on the reliable tape, price stretched above VWAP, climax volume, resistance wall within 0.3 %. `setup_short.decide` now also allows S2 / S3 (switch `SETUP_S2_S3_SHORT_ENABLED`, behind `SETUP_S2_ENABLED` / `SETUP_S3_ENABLED`), reads the facts once and stamps the match with side SHORT; without a negative event only S2 / S3 can fire. **Own cells:** a short S2 / S3 is keyed `S2_RS_BREAKOUT_SHORT|slot` (`setup_stats.cell_id` / `cell_key`), never mixed with the long cell, in `summarize`, the slot ladder (promotion / demotion), the learned time stop and the momentum exit; long cells and old stamps are unchanged, and the round 43 learned short target may now read these cells. **Kept narrow:** only an S4 short earns the 09:21 early window, the Board-gate skip and the squeeze-guard exemption; an S2 / S3 short is sized by the engine (half, quarter in the 09:20 slot), and every other gate runs as before. `setup_engine.py` is untouched (shared copy with real-trade-service stays identical). Tests: `tests/test_e274_short_s2_s3.py` (20).
- **E274 round 45 (31 Oct 2026): a fresh negative event on a stock Real Trade holds sells it or tightens its stop (real-trade-service).** **Found:** the plan says S4 is the exit trigger for a held stock in Real Trade (long only), but nothing checked open positions against the typed event feed: the negative-event veto only stopped new longs. **Fixed:** new `exit_engine/event_exit.py` (pure) and `intraday_news.negative_event(db, symbol, opened_at)` (today's market-hours snapshot, only an event announced after the entry; or the after-hours / pre-open veto row, only for a position opened on an earlier day; cached 60 s, fail-open). Exit loop step 3c: strength >= 0.60 sells (reason `event_exit`, any P&L), 0.40 to 0.60 raises the stop to just under the price (0.25 x ATR, or 0.5 % without ATR, rounded down to the tick, never lowered); never before 09:20. Switches: `EVENT_EXIT_MODE` (off | tighten | exit, default exit), `EVENT_EXIT_MIN_STRENGTH`, `EVENT_EXIT_STRONG_STRENGTH`, `EVENT_EXIT_TIGHT_ATR`, `EVENT_EXIT_START_IST`, `EVENT_EXIT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES`; three in the control catalog. Sell uses the existing `_send_real_sell` (market). Not done: limit-order exit at 09:20 for an after-hours event and a positive event extending the time stop. Tests: `tests/test_e274_event_exit.py` (9, run).
- **E274 round 46 (31 Oct 2026): the exit for after-hours news on a held stock is a limit sell, not a market sell (real-trade-service).** **Found:** round 45 sold a held stock at MARKET on a strong negative event; the plan says a limit order at 09:20 for news that came after hours, so the gap open is not sold into a thin book. **Fixed:** `event_exit.limit_price_for` gives last price minus `EVENT_EXIT_LIMIT_BUFFER_PCT` (default 0.5 %), rounded DOWN to the tick, only when the event source is the after-hours / pre-open row; the exit loop sends it as a LIMIT `event_exit` sell through the existing `_send_real_sell`. A market-hours event stays MARKET. Safety: the existing exit-limit expiry pass cancels an unfilled one after `EXIT_LIMIT_VALIDITY_MINUTES` (3) and resends the remainder as MARKET; a new `_event_exit_order_pending` stops a second sell while the first is working. Switch `EVENT_EXIT_LIMIT_ENABLED` (default on; off = always MARKET), in the control catalog. Tests: `tests/test_e274_event_exit.py` (10, run). Still not done: a positive event extending the time stop.
- **E274 round 47 (31 Oct 2026): Real Trade's morning swing pass buys event-backed picks first and refuses a pick with a fresh negative event (real-trade-service).** **Found:** the swing entry (limit order from 09:21, open-reversal skip, gap and sector checks) already existed, but it ranked picks by scan rank only and never looked at the typed event feed. **Fixed:** `intraday_news.positive_event_any` (today's market-hours positive event, else the after-hours / pre-open row tagged p=+1; fail-open) and `swing/lane.order_event_first` (backed picks first, stronger event first, scan rank inside each group; pure) order the day's picks in `swing/live.entries`; the same pass now calls `event_veto_reason` per pick and skips with `EVENT_VETO: ...` (it did not before for the swing lane). The entry Telegram message shows the event type and strength. Switches `SWING_EVENT_FIRST_ENABLED` and `SWING_EVENT_VETO_ENABLED` (default on, in the control catalog). Tests: `tests/test_e274_swing_event_first.py` (4, run). Not run here: the live `entries` path (needs the real stack). Still not done in Real Trade: a positive event extending the time stop, results-date handling against the hold window, 5-minute momentum exits, setup-based time stops, heat with a gap allowance.
- **E274 round 48 (31 Oct 2026): a swing position in profit is checked for fading momentum on 5-minute bars during the session (real-trade-service).** **Found:** `exit_engine/momentum_health.py` (shared, identical copy) was only wired in Position Stocks; Real Trade's swing lane exited on its stop, the 15:00 re-check and the structure rule only. **Fixed:** new `exit_engine/swing_momentum.py` rolls today's cached 1-minute bars (`orb_bars`, never waits for the network) into complete 5-minute bars from the later of the entry and 09:15, hands them to `momentum_health.decide` (with the forming bar, because `decide` ignores the last row) and returns HOLD / TIGHTEN / BOOK. Real Trade has no tape and no VWAP-fade feed, so the signals that can fire are no_new_best (90 min without a new high), climax_bar and at_wall; 2 signals raise the stop (never lowered), 3 signals plus 1 % profit sell (`momentum_exit`, market). Exit loop step 3d: swing positions only, in profit, 09:45 to 15:00 IST, once a minute per position, at least 6 complete bars, stale bars = no opinion. Switches: `SWING_MOMENTUM_EXIT_MODE` (off | tighten | exit, default exit, in the control catalog), `SWING_MOMENTUM_BOOK_N`, `_MIN_PROFIT_PCT`, `_MIN_BARS`, `_NO_NEW_BEST_MIN`, `_GAP_MIN_PCT`. - **E276 round 61 (1 Nov 2026): the heat decision, made - the stage 0 total open-risk limit stays at 5 % in both services; no code change, comments and plan updated.** The plan asked to choose between raising the stage 0 heat limit (6 to 8 %) and keeping it and accepting smaller per-trade risk at five positions. **Kept at 5 %.** Reasons: (1) the live base is already 5 % (`DEFAULT_MAX_PORTFOLIO_RISK_PCT` in Real Trade, `HEAT_LIMIT_PCT` in Position Stocks), not the 4 % the plan assumed, so stage 0 is not tighter than today and the plan's 'never lower than today' rule holds; (2) 5 to 6 % of equity is the usual ceiling on total open risk (Elder's 6 % rule, the 5 to 6 % range Van Tharp's heat teaching works in), so 5 % is at the conservative end of the convention and 6 to 8 % would be above it before any edge is shown; (3) the edge is unproven (entry source -0.11 % net at 60 minutes, realized P&L about -4.5 % of the pool), and raising the ceiling only raises how fast a bad run drains the pool; (4) the daily-loss cap (3 % Real Trade, 4 % Position Stocks) sits below the heat limit, so a base above 5 % would let open risk exceed what one bad day is allowed to lose. **What 5 % means on the Rs 7,288 pool:** about Rs 364, so two full 2 % trades (about Rs 146 each) and a half; the five slots fill only when conviction scales risk down to about 1 % a trade. The ladder still raises the limit by 1 point per stage with evidence (6 % at stage 1, 7 % at stage 2, 8 % at stage 3). **Half-Kelly at stage 3 is NOT built, on purpose:** the 3 % per-trade ceiling is below half-Kelly for any realistic edge on this pool, so the ceiling always binds and the formula would change nothing. Plan item 'Real Trade 3 to 5 positions' was already done in E273 round 22 (`DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS` = 5); the swing lane keeps SWING_MAX_POSITIONS 2 and SWING_PICKS_PER_DAY 2.

- **E272 round 11 (31 Oct 2026): a fresh negative event now pulls an OPEN trade's stop in (position-stocks).** The held-position half of the plan's E272 live effect, which round 10 left open. New `orders/event_hook.py`, one pass per fast-reconcile cycle in `main.py`, right after the tape hook and before the stop watchdog. For every OPEN Super Order position (not an overnight CNC carry) it reads `GET /events/{symbol}/active` (cached `EVENT_HELD_CACHE_S` 60 s per symbol) and takes the strongest event with a known polarity. When that event is AGAINST the trade (negative on a long, positive on a short), was announced AFTER the trade opened (an event known at entry, or one with no usable announce time, never counts), and has strength >= `EVENT_HELD_MIN_STRENGTH` (0.4), the stop moves so only (1 - `EVENT_HELD_TIGHTEN_FRAC`) (0.5) of its distance behind the live price remains, rounded to the tick. Pure `decide` refuses: no event, unknown polarity, wrong polarity, too weak, known at entry, the same event already used, a stop on the wrong side of the price (the stop watchdog's case), a result no tighter than the current stop, or one that would sit at or past the price. The leg is changed with `modify_super_order(STOP_LOSS_LEG)` and read back with `verify_stop_leg`; an unconfirmed or rejected modify leaves the stored stop alone and retries next cycle. On success `stop_moved_to_breakeven` is set so breakeven.py can never lower it, and `flow_json["event_tighten"]` (last 10: time, event time and type, strength, ltp, old and new stop) is stamped; each event (by announce time) tightens a trade once. The multiple scales the old budget in `capital/ledger.reserve_capital(conviction_mult=...)` AFTER the slot cap. *Real Trade* (`entry_engine/conviction_size.py`): candidate conviction 0.35, board 0.20, reward:risk 0.15, regime strength vs its gate 0.15, entry freshness (drift vs ATR limit) 0.15; the multiple moves risk_engine's two RUPEE caps (concentration 5c and max trade value 5c-ii) through `OrderIntent.size_mult / size_ceiling_pct`, REAL only. Score <= 35 -> x0.5, 50 -> x1.0 (an entry with nothing known scores exactly 50 = the old size), >= 80 -> x3.0. **Safety:** an unknown input is neutral and can never lift a score (fewer than two known inputs = the old size); an upsize never takes more than 50 % of the service's pool / equity (`CONVICTION_MAX_POOL_PCT` / `CONVICTION_MAX_POSITION_PCT`), never exceeds the plain per-trade risk at the trade's own stop (Position Stocks), is never below the old size, and is HELD at x1.0 on a losing day (`CONVICTION_NO_UPSIZE_ON_LOSS_DAY`), in a regime override, and while a VIX / calendar / opening-window size-down is in force (Real Trade, because those scale the share count before the rupee caps). Real Trade's per-trade RISK cap, cash, 50 % capital-share cap, portfolio risk cap, daily-loss caps and loss-streak brake, and every Position Stocks step after sizing (depth / VIX / calendar / opening size-down, ENTRY_MIN_QTY, cost gate, kill switches, shared order budget) are unchanged. A smaller multiple can leave fewer shares than ENTRY_MIN_QTY, which then waits instead of taking a 1-2 share trade. Targets and stops are not changed: reward:risk stays the adaptive 1:2 floor up to the target cap. Every entry logs `conviction N -> xM size` with the parts, and the Telegram BUY message and the Real Trade PLACED event carry the same line. **Switches** (all live on the Real Money Calibration page, Money safety; protected from the auto-calibrator): `CONVICTION_SIZING_ENABLED` (false = the old fixed size), `CONVICTION_MAX_MULT`, `CONVICTION_SHORT_MAX_MULT` (Position Stocks), `CONVICTION_MIN_MULT`, `CONVICTION_MAX_POOL_PCT` / `CONVICTION_MAX_POSITION_PCT`, `CONVICTION_SCORE_LOW / MID / HIGH`, `CONVICTION_NO_UPSIZE_ON_LOSS_DAY`. The maths file `conviction_sizing.py` has two byte-identical copies (checked by `scripts/check_shared_copies.py`). **Tests:** new `tests/test_e266_conviction_sizing.py` in both services (maths, ledger budget and ceilings, scoring, risk-engine caps with every other limit still binding, a real `attempt_entry` buying more for a sure setup); older tests run with the feature off through an autouse fixture (as for E252); `tests/test_short_live.py`, `tests/test_regime_hooks.py` pins and `scripts/test_short_live.py` fakes updated for the new `conviction_mult` argument. **Not run:** nothing against live Dhan; watch the `conviction` log lines for a few sessions before raising `CONVICTION_MAX_MULT`. A bigger position wins more and loses more by the same factor.

The same burst was seen on 29 Oct (E253, slow Oracle, DPY-4024); fail-closed itself is kept on purpose (two services, one Dhan account). **Changes (position-stocks only):** (1) a database-driver error (sqlalchemy `DBAPIError` incl. `DatabaseError` / `OperationalError`, a pool `TimeoutError`, `PendingRollbackError`) is retried `SYMBOL_LOCK_DB_RETRIES` times (default 1) after a rollback and a pause of `SYMBOL_LOCK_DB_RETRY_DELAY_S` (0.3 s) x attempt; only when the retry fails too does the gate fail closed as before (CRITICAL log, rate-limited Telegram, exits never gated). Programming errors are not retried; `SYMBOL_LOCK_DB_RETRIES=0` = the old behaviour; `SHARED_GATES_FAIL_CLOSED=false` still fails open. (2) a "table does not exist" error (ORA-00942 / Postgres UndefinedTable) re-creates `stockky_shared_symbol_lock` with `checkfirst` (never ALTERs; at most once per 5 min) before the retry. (3) the Telegram alert now carries the first line of the driver message (e.g. `DatabaseError: ORA-00942 ...`) so the cause is visible without opening the log. **Not changed:** `capital/shared_order_budget.py` and real-trade-service's copies of both gates have the same fail-closed shape and no retry yet. **If the alert keeps coming:** the retry only covers blips; read the new alert text or the `try_claim(...) failed (attempt N)` log line with its traceback for the ORA code (a permanent error such as a bad credential, a missing grant or a full tablespace needs fixing in the database, not in code). **Tests:** new `tests/test_e265_symbol_lock_retry.py` (12) pass here against the real `shared_symbol_lock.py` with stand-ins for sqlalchemy / models; the existing `tests/test_shared_symbol_lock.py` and the full suite were NOT run (sqlalchemy / pytest not installed here) - run `bash scripts/docker_test.sh position-stocks-service`. `docs/ENV_REFERENCE.txt` regenerated.
